I cannot live under those tyrants.
I understand. I will give you the only freedom I can.
I would rather die than go back!
You fought well, Nashta. I am proud of you.

This was the best end I could have wished for Nashta. I think it was what she always wanted: not to live under the heavy oppression of a rigid set of rules, but to die fighting, as a true <i>{dekhara}. In death, by standing and fighting, she has cleared her shame. She will be remembered as a woman filled with the irrepressible spirit of the warrior, one with so much aggression that she had no place in this civilised world.\r\n\r\nI will retrieve her body. Leave me now. I have some final things to say to my sister that are not for a <i>{jingakh} to hear. Go well, my friend.

Nenet is from a people that currently call themselves the Faridun. They are our rejects. Those we Maraketh left to die in the desert as children for being unworthy or flawed. I do not think ill of Nenet. I do not think of her at all.\r\n\r\nI am not cruel, exile. It is simply that scattered groups of pariahs wandering in the desert have no effect on the world. She will not find the home she yearns for among these scoundrels.

I prefer not to name my <i>{akhara} in the presence of these persons of ill repute, but I can say that I am from the northern reaches of the Plains of Vastiri. My home caravan has ninety-two carts, all of which are beautifully set with colourful tapestries and shaped metal. It is a life and land unlike this one. Difficult, duty-bound, but rewarding. I will return there someday, when my duty here is at an end.\r\n\r\nI still owe a debt to the Boss for allowing me a place here. Nashta may be dead, but I will stay here for a few more moons.
This way, Mr Tibbs. A warm bath awaits you.
We are not strangers. Countless bubbles.
It appears you met great success.
I am pleased for you, Mr Tibbs.
Left any children to die lately, Maraketh?
Not personally. I prefer to cook and eat them.
So you admit you are evil!
Why do you hide your face, Faridun?
Certainly it cannot be that bad?
My own mother was willing to abandon me over it.
The desert is a harsh Sekhema.
Have I ever told you that your mind is incredibly ordered?
Or oppression. I know a little about that.
Niles, do you still reject the gods?
You cannot reject that which does not exist!
You've got fire magic, don't you, Adiyah?
I do. I use it sparingly.
Where do you draw it from? Is it in the palms? The fingers? If your hand were accidentally severed, could it still light a flame?
I prefer not to answer that.
How did your explosions fare, Vinderi?
They went off with a bang! Which was quite a lot quieter than I'd intended, actually...
You've got quite the stature, Adiyah. Have you ever considered acting?
Always happy to see your portals, Adiyah. And... Call me Huck.
Adiyah, you've never looked more lovely. Take us home, yeah?
Of course. It is my duty.
Did it go as planned? Any injuries? Karst?
I'm fine, beautiful! Top o' the world!
You've no tattoos, Maraketh. Have you ever fought a battle?
I do not have tattoos, Karui, because they are marks of shame or criminality.

Round here, people call me Tibbs. Not the quietest little sneak, and I'm not exactly nimble with these big sausage fingers, but if you find yourself on the wrong side of something heavy, you'll wish you thought to hire me.

Heard the Boss got his start as a stable boy in the Grand Arena. Used to feed and care for the chariot horses. That was his first job, and it led to his first ... err, 'job'. 

Apparently, someone asked him to slip something into the feed of the Octavius family's finest stallion, greatly favoured to win the race. Paid him a week's worth of his normal wages. Boss figured it was some sort of poison. So he watched the man place a bet, and poisoned that horse as well. Neither died, but neither won, and the Boss, betting his wages on a horse he knew to be fit as a gladiator, took home a killing. 

'Course, that was also his last day of gainful employment at the arena. The man stalked those stables for months trying to find him.

Ah, my contract! A man of my build gets a lot of attention. By the time I was thirteen, I was taller than most adults. By my next birthday I was invited to join a little circus of sorts as the strongman. That's where I met Tullina, by the way.

One day, someone left a baby girl, named Opal, for the troupe leader. She had bright red eyes, but the most pale skin and whitest hair I'd ever seen. She became a sort of daughter of the whole troupe. We took turns looking after her. 

By the time she was about seven, I'd grown quite attached to her, and she to me. The hardest part of being exiled is not knowing what has happened to her. So I want to find out. I know the troupe is disbanded, so I just want to make sure she's found a good home.

Well, it ain't great news. Templar took an interest in her because of her unique traits, but she dropped off the map before they could get her. Good instincts. \r\n\r\nI have a hunch that she might've found some of the old troupe members. I'll see what Whakano can dig up.

Got an update on Opal! She's living on the fringes with some of the old troupe, like I thought. Tough people to track down, but at least I know she's safe. \r\n\r\nI want to keep it that way. I want to make sure she doesn't need to put herself at risk to work or eat, so we're going to do what is, essentially, the opposite of a bank robbery. We're breaking in to leave enough wealth for her to live safely out of harm's way in a vault under a pseudonym.

I know I'm a lot poorer than I was a few days ago, but I feel like I've done some real good. Opal's a smart kid. She'll put that money to good use. Better than I would've anyway.\r\n\r\nThanks, Exile. Really.
Just don't ask me to help you move.
Hey, as long as I don't have to do any of the planning...
Lemme jus' get this outta the way for ya.
Oh, I'm going to be sore tomorrow.
If it ain't broke, it will be...
This one might take a bit, but we'll get there.
I think it'd look better in pieces too.
In the middle of something here.
When I'm done with this, yeah?
Hate this part of the job.
You're gonna be sorry. Then I'm gonna be sorry.
Right, well, carry on I guess.
Now who just leaves something like that lying around?
Oh, know a girl who'd love that.
I'm gettin' a bad feeling, mate.
Reckon we're cutting it close now.
Right, we gotta make tracks soon.
Now you've gone and done it.
Think this might be what we're after.
Right, let's nab it and go.
Here we go. Make it quick.
Now we just gotta make it out alive!
Always get butterflies before a job...
Whew, I'm sweating. Just nerves. Just harmless nerves.
I always think this time I won't get nervous, and I always do.
Come on, Gil. You've got this. Easy as. Eeeaaasy as.
You ever get the feeling--... Nah. Nevermind.
We bloody did it mate! We bloody did it!
Yes! I'm comin' home with the goods!
Honestly, for a while there, I thought we were done for.
I'ma be sore tomorrow for sure! Good sore.
I'll do my best, but damn!
I'm taking the longest, bubbliest damn bath after this!
This is gonna leave a mark!
I can't work under these conditions!
\"Go on Tibbs, you're a big guy!\"
Part of the job. Part of the job.
Better be worth the delay, mate!
Your greed better not get us killed!
That's our mark! Grab it and go!
Why would you say that!? Now you've definitely jinxed us.
Stick to the plan and this'll be quick and easy.
That's genius! If we make the plan sticky, we're less likely to drop it. I'll jot that down!
Reddy! I'd always wondered what your first name was. Teddy Ribbs. Got it.
It never goes as bad as you expect. Remember that.
I expect us all to die. Any better than that is a victory.
Check your gear, say a prayer, whatever you need to do before we go in.
A prayer? I might as well ask the Solstice Rhoa for an albino egg! Equally absurd!
Remember the target. Don't get too sidetracked.
Sound advice for life in general, really.
Safety first. If it gets too dangerous, leave.
Helps to know you're looking out for us, Tibbs.
Try not to hit your head on the way in, ay big boy?
Thanks for the... heads up! ... Nothing?
There is death on the wind. Beware.
Not the sort of thing I like hearing before a job.
Tibbs, could you please lower your anxiety? It's seeping into my brain.
Maybe you shouldn't be snooping around in there.
What's the rule, everyone? Be efficient, and...?
How's my scary voice? You there! I'll break you in half!
Ehh... Sorry Gianna. Maybe practice that one more.
Can't believe we pulled that off. Even Karst did good!
Tibbs, are you left or right handed?
So the evil reflection is still at large...
I think we've all earned an evening off.
And if anyone else gets sad when they're alone with their thoughts, I'll be at the bar!
I had a terrible feeling about this earlier. So glad I was wrong.
The day is not done yet. Our 'friends' back home might backstab us to take our spoils.
That could've gone a lot worse!
And of course it was because of some god's intervention, right? So predictable.
...what did I even say to warrant that? Honestly.
Nearly more loot than I can carry!
Good job everyone, let's head back.
Thanks for keeping us all safe, big guy.
Good stuff! Let's celebrate! First round is on Tibbs!
Fine, but you're only getting pondwater, Karst.
Barely any malfunctions and plenty of data.
Gods I feel so young again! Tibbs! Let me lift you up!
I believed we would face our deaths in there. I am glad to have been wrong.
Wait... You thought we were going to die?
And you didn't want to tell us?
I did not see the need.
This was a wondrous return to the glory days of the Templars.
Well, all the killing and mind-crushing. It was... nostalgic.
Gravicius himself couldn't have planned a better operation.
You've set the bar pretty low, mate.
We did it! Three cheers! Hip-hip?
Heard you could use a bit of muscle!
The Boss is always happy to have you involved, Tibbs. How are your nerves?
Every time, I think I might get used to the stress, but...
I understand. Please look after yourself.
That includes physically. You start feeling the wear and tear of the work, you tell me, understood?
Do we have to do this every time?
Oh c'mon. Just havin' a little fun.
Tibbs is so tall, that he... uh... He's so tall, that...
Just wait. He's so tall... that...
... Look how tall Tibbs is everyone!
Good try, champ. Now we grownups can focus on the job.
The usual. Steal ALL of the THINGS!
My favourite kind. You bringing any new gadgets with us?
Afraid not. The bone decoupler decoupled itself. The test bone is fine, though there are now several thin metal strips deeply embedded in it.
Gave me an idea for intra-muscular springs. Tibbs, would you like to test something with me after this job?
Tight! Ribs! Err, right! Tibbs! I've got a new formula for you to try.
Just like the last one, but I've enriched the quicksilver with Chimeral blood. Really gives it a kick.
Just don't give it an actual kick.
Good. I won't. Thank you for the warning.
I always worry I'm late, even when I'm early.
You worry about much. Why is that?
That... is a really tough question to answer.
I never worry, because the worst has already happened to me. This isn't even my life. It's just a shadow. Do you worry about stepping on your shadow?
Wow, Nenet, you're really quite profound. Anyone ever told you that?
Not my mother, that's for certain.
Are you sure? Are there no... large words I should explain to you?
Niles, do you think I'm stupid because I'm strong?
You think that a strong man cannot be a smart man, eh? The two are somehow mutually exclusive?
You're a mindreader, right? How about you jump on in here and have a look around.
I-... I rescind my statement. I apologise for my preconceived notions.
Joining us on this job, Tibbs?
That's a relief, honestly. Normally I'm the largest target.
Ha! You're still a plenty big target.
I look like Kurai next to you!
Tibbie! Always love a job with you.
Thanks Gi. How was your date with--
Uhh, yeah, that was... a mistake.
Well, let's just say he looked a lot more than he listened.
Ah. Well, always more men in the sea.
Thanks, Ku. How's the Boss doing?
Busy. Stressed. Worried for the safety of those in his care.
Oh! You're workin' this job too?
Yeah? Wait, what did you--... No, you know what, nevermind.
Guess the blood struggles to get all the way up to 'is brain, eh? eh?
Made it! Had to put out a small fire, but I made it.
No, sadly someone beat me to that invention a long while ago. And this particular fire completely engulfed my heat-powered-exo-strider.

Exo-strider. Yes. Put a few burning embers in the converter and off you stride! Just a prototype made of cheap materials, scrap metal, wood, oil-soaked rags--oh, dammit, Isla! You're better than this.

Never better, never better. Spent the last hour in a very enclosed space with far more voltaxic sulphite than I've ever laid eyes on before, and I must say, I do not see what all the fuss was about. So, what's this we're looking at. Some sort of cuboid creature? Where's the heart?
Did it step in paint? Can we just trace the prints back and find its nest?
Ah! A job! I see it now. Yes. Good. This means I'll need to prepare more sulphite.
I see you also, large man. These plans appear adequate.
Thank you, Nenet. Can you be of service?
Always for you, lady Kurai. It would be a great honour.
Mister Tibbs, do you ache in your large skeleton?
I'm here, no need to make a fuss.
And to you. You know, I've always wondered, where do you get your clothes?
Actually, I make them myself. Started sewing at a young--
Fascinating. To see a man of your stature wield a sewing needle must truly be something to behold.
I mean, I can show y--
Hey mate. Hey, how come you're always in your armour, even around here?
Ah, blackguard training. Never leave yourself undefended. I used to sleep with my blackguard kit on. Got to the point where I couldn't sleep without it.
You sleep with that armour on too?
Hah, no, no... I've a lighter chainmail for bedtime.
Fingers crossed this one goes better than our sewer scrape, eh, Tibbie?
I've got a change of clothes laid out just in case.
Did you ever find out where those busts were?
That was a lot of platinum!
Could've bought an island with that platinum.

'Ello rookie! Found a few markers, did ya? Apparently the Boss sees somethin' in you, but we won't know for sure 'til you're on the wrong side of a lance. I'm Karst, and there's not a lock in this world that I can't open. All you have to do is make sure I live long enough to open 'em. Adiyah'll get us to the job, and I'll show ya the ropes. Don't get tangled in 'em, 'cause it ain't my job to cut you free.

First things first; Client wants us to find an urn. Reckons the mark has it locked up. Thing is, it's pretty suspicious if that's the only thing that goes missing. Not really our problem, but taking heat off the client makes us look good, and we get to keep whatever else we find. Get where I'm going with this?
I'll pick any locks that get in our way. You keep me alive, yeah?
Hear that? We ain't alone. Place is crawling with guards. You're here to make sure they don't kill us both.
Consider your actions, yeah? We don't want too much attention.
Urn's on the other side of this door. Grab it so we can get out of here.
Perfe--... Wait, hear that? We've been made. Grab what ya can and head out.
Back the way we came, rookie!
We're still breathin, rook, so you ain't done half bad. Take that urn to Faustus, yeah? He'll sort you out.
I'm Karst. Rather than waste my youth readin', I put that time to better use. Now I can pick just about any lock you're likely to come across.

A man of style, the Boss. A thief of course wants to be rich and live a life of luxury, but once you hit a certain point of wealth, I imagine you might be motivated by other things.

Apparently, the Boss was living very comfortably indeed, but felt the need to challenge himself. He entered the First Bank of Theopolis in the middle of the day, entered the vault, and just started... movin' stuff around. Octavius family fortunes into the Maxius deposit box, Avarius riches split across every small safe, each of which he popped open as if there weren't even a lock on 'em. Mixing all the money up like it were caught in the tides. Then he goes and finds the records of deposits and withdrawals, and sets 'em on fire. Walks out like nothing happened.

Well, of course the bank puts the fire out, but the records are gone. So they notify all the big customers, telling them to come in with their copy of the deposit slips... and wouldn't you know it, they're gone too. 

No bloody idea how he pulled it off. 'Course, the bank and all the clients will deny it ever happened. Be foolish not to.

Got my contract, do ya? Ran with some low-life criminal scum in the back alleys of Oriath in my younger days. Real good blokes. Loyal to the last, or so I thought. Right before I was exiled, they beat me half to death and took off with my finest lock picks. If I'd had 'em when the Law came for me, I probably wouldn't be here, so in a sense, I 'spose I should be thankful, eh?\r\n\r\nWell I'm not. I want those picks back, and I spent a lot of markers to find out where they went. Now I know, and you're gonna help me get 'em.
Strange. I thought having these picks back would make me feel whole again, but... \r\n\r\nWell, it's not your problem, rookie. Not yet.

Been good having my old picks back. Real good. Just not good enough. It's like there's a lock inside me, and not even my beautiful antique picks can open it. But I been thinkin' about it long and hard, and I reckon I know what might.

Revenge.

One of me old crew recently got out of the game. Livin' a life of luxury now while everyone around him is suffering and strugglin' just to survive. That should've been my life, but he took it from me when he took my picks. I want to send him, and the rest of my old crew, a message. So, rather than take something, we're going to leave something. Something that'll put the fear of Sin into the lot of 'em.

Bet you're wondering what happens now, eh? Interesting little toxin we left. Slowly fills the air, then the lungs. Never leaves the body. Just keeps building up. First you start feeling light headed. Then you start hearing things, start seeing things. Start getting paranoid. A day or two later, you feel tingly. The tingling turns to pain, and the pain keeps building until your heart just stops beating.\r\n\r\nI'd wash your hands if I was you.

Word of our last job has started gettin' round. Unfortunately, all the credit is goin' to an old rival of ours. That don't sit right with me. It's one thing to steal a man's property, but to steal a man's hard work? No, I ain't gonna let that stand.\r\n\r\nSo we're going to leave a little present at my ol' rival's abode. One of my prized lockpicks, dipped in the very same toxin.

You know what, rookie? I do believe I feel whole again. It's only a matter of time 'til that old rival of mine suffers the same fate as my traitorous crewmate. With both the bastards dead, and my pick the only common thread, the message is crystal clear:\r\n\r\nDon't steal from a thief.
Forgot to tell ya, bringing this lug with us on this job.
He's an absolute nutter. Ain't ya Huck?
Not really? I suppose the Blackguard training did leave me a bit... rough.
Just keep me alive. I'll do the rest.
Hope this ain't all on me.
Just don't get in my way.
They're hiding something. I know it.
Curiosity always gets the better of me...
Love the smell of hot metal.
The more they try to keep me out, the more I want to get in.
Trying to concentrate on something else.
Can't work while I'm gettin' hit.
Any chance you could stop hitting me?
Let you get this one, yeah?
Who put you in a bad mood?
Quick, before they make too much noise.
I got the best of ya.
If you don't want it, I'll take it.
Ehh, reckon I'll find something better.
Plenty more where that came from, I reckon.
You trying to get us caught?
Oh boy, this is gonna get messy.
You hear that? That's your fault.
Great, now the whole bloody world's coming after us.
Got us here safe 'n' sound, didn't I?
Almost there. Don't screw it up.
I think this is what we're here for.
Tuck it away somewhere safe. We gotta move quick.
Aw, I wanted to hold it. Fine. Whatever. Let's just go.
Is it just me or is this as good as it gets?
Job done, right? Out we go.
Always get nostalgic before a job. Almost miss me ol' crew.
Reckon I'll have a night out with the lads after this one. Can't remember the last time I blacked out.
You're pretty quiet, eh Exile? ... Yeah, you're pretty quiet. Good quality in a thief.
If it starts gettin' hairy in there, you can handle yourself, yeah?
Things start going south in there, don't expect me to save you.
He does it again! Can anyone stop him! I sure bloody hope not.
And with that, the rookie was forever indebted to the mighty Karst!
Hope you didn't leave anything down there rook! We ain't going back!
Ahh, my lovely Adiyah! How about a celebratory drink, on me.
This one may've taken a few weeks off my life, but it was bloody worth it.
I'll try to make it quick!
You do your job, I'll do mine!
I can't see--... wait, what's that!?
Horrible time to just be standing 'round!
Nothing motivates like a little pressure!
Better lead to an escape hatch!
Can't do it all at once!
You get hit in the head?! I'm busy!
I'll fight you! I'll bloody do it, mate!
I get it, but is now the best time!?
Yeah, okay, I wouldn't have let that one go either!
I better not die because you needed that!
Get the bloody thing and let's move!
Pocket the goods! We gotta go!
Oi Isla, what was that word again
Yeah. Let's keep it clamdestine, everyone.
Vin, make sure you don't blow any powder near me, yeah?
Of course. Last time was an anomaly, I swear.
That you felt compelled to say this does not fill me with confidence.
Gods I hope this goes smoothly.
No gods will ensure success. That's up to us.
Things go south in there, it's everyone for themselves.
Stay loose. Think on your toes.
Got a new word for you, Karst. Taciturn. It means silent.
Here goes. ...Hear that? No? Taciturn, but deadly.
Wish you'd pay that much attention to me.
Confidence, not cockiness, will ensure success.
Confidence, not cockiness, will ensure success.
That is always what an interrogator wanted to hear: his own words repeated back to him with desperation.
Focus up everyone. Job comes first.
Not according to the rumours I heard about you.
Was there a script? I didn't get one.
New materials to experiment with! I'll turn gold into lead!
You tryin' to make me angry?
Dunno 'bout you, but I'm ready to go home and celebrate.
Celebrate what? What did I miss?
See that, Nenet? See what you're missin' out on?
I see everything. Flaws and all.
Make way, Adiyah. Karst needs to pray at the altar of beer.
At last, a belief system I can get behind.
Honestly didn't think we'd make it.
Honestly kind of wish you didn't. Sorry. Too mean. Sorry.
Anyone got a quill? Had an idea on the run out of here.
Oi, give your big brain a break, yeah? You earned it.
Wait, is this where we came in?
Success, but still room for improvement.
Nothin's ever good enough for you, eh?
Our persistence is rewarded. Even the supposed gods couldn't--
Messy in parts, Karst, but we got there.
Will you be gracing us with your presence on this job?
Can you make sure I get an extra cut then?
I, uh, dunno what you're on about.
The book! Did you get to the end?
Alright, no need to harp on about it. Mosty pictures, anyway.
Yeah, but it's a great start!
I said drop it, yeah? Don't need you lot thinkin' I'm the sort of person who reads a book for fun.
Oi oi! Knew Vindy'd be on this one. Could smell him from upstairs!
Ah! Yes! What you're smelling is actually a new powder blend I'm trialling. Eggs and decaying meat, yes?
Fish!? ...Fish. Ah! Right! I've also brought a fish.
The new blend. You bring a fish to hide the smell?
Nenet has as much a role as you. Leave personal grievances at the door.
And your money, if you intend to cheat at cards against me.
You should have known, with my sharp eyes...
Lockpick. I don't make 'em, I break 'em.
Of course. My apologies. I sense ...animosity.
Oh, what an incredible power! How ever does he do it?
I'll show you a well-honed talent.
Karst, have you paid Huck back yet?
Debts must be repaid. You know that. I'll garnish your fee for this job.
Keep it in your tights, Karst.
How about you an' I get ourselves a refreshing beverage after this job, ay? My treat.
That depends... Are you expecting something in return?
Only the company of a beautiful young woman.
I don't think Nenet is all that interested.
Oh Karst, you're such a good thief! You can take anything... but a hint.
Thank you for coming, Karst. Please make sure you pay attention.
Pay attention. I don't want a repeat of last time.
Fine, fine. In my defense, the term bust is really misleading.
When have you ever seen a pair of stone breasts on display?
Fair point, Lady Kurai. Fair point.
'Ere she is! Come to bore all the guards to sleep?
No, the brain-bore still requires a few small optimisations.
Oh! Sorry! You were making a joke! Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha-ha-ha!
... Isla, you making a drill for people's heads?
What? No! It's already made. I'm just tweaking it a little.
'Ello Vindy. How's old age treatin' you?
Oh, you know, has its downs and ups. Still tack as a sharp though!
What?! No one mentioned Nenet joining us.
Is that going to be an issue?
My apologies, Kurai. Karst despises me, but I do not care what he thinks, and that has caused him some emotional distress.
I understand. Karst, can you still perform your tasks?
No, I'm saying I don't want you along.
I don't believe that decision is yours to make.
Indeed! Were it up to me, you would be forever at my side, like a loyal and adoring pup.
You say that like it's a bad thing.
That's because it is a bad thing.
Ahh, my beautiful Gianna. It seems you and I shall be reconnoitering once more!
I'm... not sure you used that word ri--
Oh! Were the roses from you?
Aww, did you get me that beautiful gown!?
... Look how tall Tibbs is everyone!

Got somethin' needs made? Or unmade? I can take 'em apart as fast as I put them together, sometimes faster. Or is it the other way 'round? I've had an idea just now for a spinning device that - oh, yes, my name is Isla. I'm an engineer. Welcome.\r\n

The Boss? Oof, it's inefficient to ask about the Boss. Believe me. You'll go round and round, a spinning gear 'na machine made of secret parts. The one thing you should never rely on is a mechanism you don't understand. It's liable to implode, or <i>{ex}plode. Neither is pretty when your arse is sittin' upon it hopin' to fly somewhere. The Boss put in an order for an air-sail once, for a job. Impossible, I told Kurai. Turned out it worked! It just didn't go with the poor sod we hired. It stayed with us in flames while he took to the skies. He achieved a perfect parabolic arc right onto the tower we were aiming for. Survived the trip, too, judgin' by the screaming. But getting back down? Oof, the Boss never ordered a falling machine. That's on him. Gotta think things through, mind you!

<i>{You} want to work with <i>{me}? I didn't realize we were that close. This is fantastic! I'll need a partner to retrieve my early prototypes from the hands of the Templars. I made a series of precursor contraptions before I was exiled that would have led to some of my greatest achievements. If you can imagine it, my inventions could have done it... eventually.

I didn't realise who I was working for until it was too late. They seized my prototypes and exiled me for the damage I caused in the process of building them. What's a few implosions in the pursuit of progress? Or maybe it was the sea tide of acid... or the glowing rock that made people sick... oh, yes.

Care to help me steal those prototypes back?
My inventions! My babies! I missed them so much. I would never have found the proper materials to recreate them here on Wraeclast, not with all the horrific creatures roaming about. Thank you, Exile!

As I studied the prototypes you helped me retrieve, I realized that they'd already been examined... by someone else. The Templars must have lied about declaring my work heretical. They're trying to build them for their own gain! I cannot imagine what disaster they'll bring upon us if they manage to do so.

We already have the prototypes, so now we must steal the designs they created based on them. We'll need to steal the blueprints for my Extreme Warmth Beam, my Storm Wooing Rod... hmm, the Mind Sublimator... and the Unbreakable, of course! I don't claim to be the most imaginative namer, but it is what it is. They're all related, eventually intended to be part of one single superweapon, so the designs should all be in one place.

Let's go retrieve those blueprints!

We did it, Exile, at least in part. The designs for the Unbreakable were missing... I fear that they may have begun construction on it. If they complete the Unbreakable, we'll never be able to... break it. Science deserves better masters than the Templars!

My instruments have started going haywire. I believe the Templar have managed to build the Unbreakable, <i>{my} greatest achievement. Normally, I would be thrilled at seeing my work given life, but I have a feeling the Unbreakable will be used against us, not for us.\r\n\r\nIt's time to do some deconstruction. You're good at smashing things, yes? Then perhaps you can break the Unbreakable.
Stop, in the name of science!
My baby... my proudest work... Wait! I still have the blueprints! Let's go, Exile!
The Unbreakable has been broken. You know what that means, don't you?\r\n\r\nThe Templar didn't build it right. I'll have to continue my work to prove it can be done!
My mental gears are already turning!
Long as I can bring my gadgets.
Just tell me where to build!
The axles and the gears go 'round and 'round...
You put the axle in, you take the ball-bearing out...
Sometimes there's an elegant solution... sometimes.
I've got just the contraption for this!
Must go faster, must go faster.
Can't think with all that racket!
Let's throw a wrench in the works.
Construction, deconstruction... it's all the same, in the end.
A beautiful design. A shame I have to wreck it.
Traps are the arse end of engineering. No artisanship.
I'm just going to smack it with a wrench!
I can't even hear myself think!
The mind is just another system of gears.
Your mental machinery is mine to mould!
I'm in the middle of something.
Aren't you supposed to defend your engineer?!
I can't think when I'm under attack!
Oh my, someone must do the fighting now.
I hope you don't expect me to fight.
A better plan would have avoided this.
Not good. Not good at all!
They should have thought this through.
If they cannot prevent us from taking it, it is ours.
A good plan reaps its own rewards.
I believe they call that loot.
The plan was to get treasure before the alarm!
Now's not the time for looting!
We get nothing if the plan fails!
Why are you doing that now?!
We're at the limits of our plan now.
This clock is on the verge of chiming...
We can afford no more unanticipated variables.
We will be detected if we are not careful.
The clock chimes at the appointed hour!
Our design appears to have been flawed!
Phase one complete. Acquire the treasure.
Remember, this is only the midpoint.
From the blueprints, I thought it'd be bigger.
I haven't even used half my contraptions yet!
Apex of the plan accomplished. Now, to survive!
A strong plan is the best path to success.
We can account for all the variables. No deviating!
I hope I get to use my contraptions.
Is this the part where we make nervous small talk?
You do know what you're doing, yes?
The real treasure is the knowledge we gleaned along the way!
Does this mean we're friends now?
Is this the part where we make relieved small talk?
Plan, execute, success! I love logic!
This has inspired an idea for a new invention!
Ah good, Isla, at least I know one person will be paying attention.
Unless you're thinking about one of your inventions.
I'm always thinking about my inventions.
I've never known you to be excited for this part, Isla.
I better be! We've only got a few hours!
It's not a major concern. The spores are currently harmless. Just have to be back to my devices before my vivarium germinates.
Hurry now, let's get the job done!
I'm here. What is that ticking noise?
Is it a tunk... tunk... tunk, or more of a tick, tick, tick?
Are you... going to check on that ticking?
Oh no, that won't go off for several hours, probably.
Oh, Nenet, there you are. I had a minor breakthrough on that humanoid golem you asked for.
Why are you bringing that up here?!
The thing is, I can't get his movement right. He's as stiff as granite, which is to be expected. Also, he doesn't cook very well.
Sands swallow me, so that I die right here...
Ah, Isla, our woman of science! It's the young ones that are wrong, not we.
The same thing I always rant about, my dear.
One of my machines detects divine energies. Divinity is real.
Your machine is broken, and so are you!
If I use two parts Voltaxic Sulphite with three parts Trarthan... oh my, who are you?
We've met a hundred times. We've gone on heists together.
Oh yes, yes, I have trouble with faces. Especially handsome faces.
Your thoughts... how vile! That is not how it works!
The human body is just another machine, my dear... joints... pistons...
You stay away from me, witch!
The new moon approaches. Shall we have that competition of explosions we spoke about?
My inventions aren't supposed to explode.
I... I don't remember. Do you?
Badwyth Nems? Is that Ezomyte? I'll write it down so I don't forget. Right under Vinderi. I think that's the tall lad.
Good, Isla's here! A unit's only as good as its engineer, I always say.
Not that I... meant anything by that...
You wanted to see me, Huck?
I'm here. Isla, will we be seeing some new inventions for this job?
But you've tested them at least, right? ...Right? ...Isla?
Can I bring my glowing red rocks along on this mission?
The ones that make people sick?
The rocks don't make people sick. It's the Corruption they leak that does that.
Wear a dress lined with six-inch-thick armour and you'll be fine.
Just what every man likes to see.
No useless prayers today. I put my faith in science!
Niles, have you thought about those interrogation devices I suggested?
There's torture, and then there's nightmare. You are a demon with a pleasant smile.
You think I've got a pleasant smile?
I'll watch your back, keep you safe.
How about you go in front instead of behind us?
It was a figure of speech.
You can rely on my contraptions, Huck! Have no fear!
Fear keeps a disciplined man alive.
I'm never going to wear that infernal thing, Isla. Stop asking, I beg of you.
Do we really need to infiltrate anything? Between you and me, Isla, we could just blow the whole thing up.
But then what would we take? Oh, the scrap! Of course!
Just remember when we're in there, combustion is the mother of invention!
Never met the lad. Knew a concubine, though. Loads of children.
You know what we could really use...?
--that focuses all the light to a white-hot point, and sets everything it touches on fire!
Or just a normal mirror! For makeup!
I'll be watching your art. I'm not great with people.
Ah, but a watched rose never blossoms, my dear.
Thank you. But seriously, if you stare at me, we WILL be caught.
Told you I'd never let anything happen to you.
Your skills and my inventions carried the day!
It is remarkable how we beat the odds when we are together.
I... I really thought we were going to cash in our Markers on that one.
Nonsense. A good plan always succeeds.
How was that according to plan?
Oops, did I not tell you the contingencies? No wonder you were terrified!
That was impressive. I should study your brain.
Can you do that without drills?
No drills, I promise. I could do it with a trepan.
At some point, after so many close calls, a man's gotta admit he's just tired.
I could replace your muscles with pistons if you like.
How about that? A second wind! I'm fine now, plenty fine.
Your chances for survival would have been much better with my Voltaxic-powered battle armour.
That thing ripped a mannequin in half!
I thought you were STRONGER than a mannequin...
Oh, I am! I-, I am!
This mission is going to be spectacular. I've got all sorts of explosives to set, and they'll never even see it coming.
We just did the mission. We're going home now.
You'll have to excuse me for a moment once we're back home, then.
What are you going to do with your share, Vinderi?
Try out new powders, of course!
No! It's MY share, and that includes any notes in it!
I have to admit, engineer, you make quite the spectacle yourself sometimes!
If I'm not making people cower in terror from the inexplicability of my inventions, then I'm not really doing science right!
I have so much to learn about science...
If I copy what you did with your art, will I have the same effect on men?
First thing I'm going to do is go terrorise Niles some more.
Normally I'd disapprove, but it's Niles, so...

Tala moana and good tidings! I'm Whakano, though most people know me as the Barber. If you need a trim and tidy then take a seat. But a little fishy told me you may be more interested in a conversation than a cut.

A man like myself, travelling around as much as I do, hears a lot of things. Everyone needs their hair cut once in a while, and I am a very attentive listener.

Some of the things I hear could be very lucrative to people with certain, shall we say, unscrupulous ambitions. 

Drop a few markers in the tip jar, and I may accidentally drop some of my meticulously well-kept notes.

Interesting man. Very interesting indeed. Hairless as the day he came into this world. No need for a man of my trade, you see. Yet, bald as he may be, he knows the value of a good barber. 

No one here knows much about the Boss's past, except maybe Kurai, and she won't tell you much, not even for a mountain of markers. Loyalty is the most valuable currency, and she and the Boss have a lifetime supply.

I tried to find out what I could. Conflicting tales of a smuggler kingpin, a Theopolan aristocrat, and, strange enough, a retired arena champion. Then Kurai told me to stop sniffing around, else I end up like the last barber. Or maybe she said I'd end up <i>{the} last barber. Either way, I value my life and my work more than I value gossiping about an old, bald, gladiatorial smuggler.

Troubling news coming out of Oriath. I know you weren't just involved, but smack-dab in the middle of things. I also know you aren't to blame. Not directly, anyway. 

Still, you might imagine that I feel some... animosity about the whole situation. Not least of all because the presence of Kitava is quite literally a doomsday scenario for my people. 

I trust you'll sort it out, 'cause if you don't, we're through. And I don't just mean no more business.

Listen, I don't want to be a nay-sayer, but before you started coming around here, we didn't have none of this god nonsense. They were just characters in stories. Ways to get the kiddos to eat their greens. And that was fine! In fact, I preferred it that way! \r\n\r\nNow? We've got characters coming to life! And then you're killing 'em! You're killing our heroes! Tukohama was one of the good guys! You better finish what you started.

Well, at least you followed through eh? I'd have preferred if my gods stayed tucked away neatly in their tales, but if we're going to have the Ravenous One up and about, at least we have you to put him back to bed for good.

The rebellion was a long time coming, if you ask me, which you did. And if you ask me, which you didn't, I reckon the bloodshed was inevitable. The gods rising up? That one, I will admit, took me by surprise. So now the Karui are sailing back home -- good. But anger has a tendency to linger like a bad smell, and the enslaved are justifiably angry. It may take a long time before that anger fades. It may never.

Let's say you're a wealthy Oriathan slave merchant. You're out there, selling people to other people, really raking in the coin off the back of racial divides. Then one day, those people you've been selling start killing the people you've been selling 'em to! That's gotta be bad for business, right? Time to cut your losses?

Sadly, no. Slavers have had their pride badly bruised. They're out there -- right now -- looking for Karui men, women, even children, and kidnapping 'em. No one's heard from the taken since. You think they're getting sold to new owners? Not a chance. They're being tortured. Murdered. The slavers see this as revenge, but it is nothing more than evil for evil's sake.

A lot of bad things have come from the rise of Kitava, but this... for me, this is the worst.

Kitava's rebirth has heralded countless tragedies, but there has been one shining light to come from it -- the unshackling of my brothers and sisters. Freed Karui slaves were among the first survivors to reach the shores of Wraeclast. I watched them kiss the sand, sing, dance. I watched them finally enjoy the freedom they should have had all along. Then it started coming unwound. \r\n\r\nA man by the name of Hapihapi who was helping the returnees resettle has gone missing. A witness claims he was taken aboard a slaver's ship. I know where that ship took him. I want you to go there. I want you to find him. I want you to free him.

Wish I was surprised by this turn of events. I really do. This is just another line on a page, in a book writ only of atrocities against the Karui people. I fear this is not some aberrant event, but is the beginning of a pattern.

I appreciate your effort, though. I will stay vigilant. I hope you do, as well.

I will send a message to Hapihapi's friends and family. They will give him an honourable send-off.

Sometimes I hate being right. Hapihapi's kidnapping was followed by a string of similar kidnappings. All Karui, some barely old enough to walk. Even in this time of madness and upheaval, as dead Oriathans are still being put to rest, slavers are taking my brothers and sisters. Different ships, but the methods they're using are too similar to be coincidence. Someone is in charge of this, and I want to know who.\r\n\r\nThe Oriath Records Office holds a lot of documents, including sales records of slaves, slaver licenses, and records of the whereabouts and ownership of every known slave. Get me those documents.
Many thanks, Exile. Leave these documents with me. I'll send a few little fishies upstream and see what they come back with.

Here's the thing about slavers; without the blessing of the Templar authorities, they collapse under pressure like a sandcastle. 

My little fishies have come back, and they've brought with them a name: Friedrich Tarollo. 

Not surprised you haven't heard of him. He was small-time. But even in a career known for callousness and cruelty, Friedrich was a real bastard. Loved the chase. Loved the struggle. Left his mark on the backs of many of my brothers and sisters.

It seems he has holed himself up in a cave somewhere, declared himself the supreme ruler of the slavers, and is enjoying the lawlessness Oriath's collapse has brought to a sickening degree. Find him and bring him to justice.

I heard the news, Exile. Tarollo is dead. The message is loud and clear to those who care to listen; the Karui people are a free people, and will not bend to threats and terror, not now, not ever.\r\n\r\nMaybe this was just a job for you, maybe it was more. I don't much care either way. What matters is that you enacted change. For that, you have earned my markers and my respect.

I heard the news, Exile. Tarollo is dead. The message is loud and clear to those who care to listen; the Karui are a free people, and will not bend to threats and terror, not now, not ever.

But what you found there... If Tarollo can use it to fuel his hate, maybe it can be used for protection. Yet... Just being near it unsettles me. I don't know what it is, but it needs to be in safe hands.

I'll hold onto it for now. I don't trust anyone else with it, not even you. Sorry... and, I suppose, thank you.
How are things aboard your ship, sir?
The Marylene? Oh, you know... Get a bunch of men in a small space and there's bound to be bickering and brawling. The ol' lashing arm's been getting a good workout, I must say.
Do they mind you spending all this time here, sir?

Well they don't exactly know I'm here, per se, but I imagine, rapscallions that they are, they savour any time where the man-in-charge is absent. In my day, we'd tie up the first mate, break into the swill, and see who could down the most before passing out or dying.
You must've met the lash when your captain came back, eh?

Oh, no. No no no. Most of us came from good, Innocence-fearing families. The captain knew that raising a hand to us would put him in hot water back home. We got away with murder, really. No, really, a few of the boys beat a galley slave to death. Barely got a talking to. Nowadays, of course, Admiral Darnaw lets damn-near anyone join the ranks. Horrible policy. I do enjoy doling out the punishments, though.
What do your people think about what happened in Oriath?
Karui! Are they dancing round their totems singing the praises of the return of their saviour?
Kitava is no saviour. Far from it. Kitava is symbolic of death, of the end of all things.
Eh? I thought that was, uh, hinny--something.
Hinekora? The Mother of Death is the steward of our souls, but she has no great desire to destroy us. It's a common misunderstanding among your people.

Captains. I cannot speak for all Karui, but personally, I feel a great sadness for Oriath. Many people lost their lives, their homes, their families. Good people. Bad people too, but even bad people should have the opportunity to reflect on their misdeeds and change. Kitava took that opportunity away.
Strange turn of events, eh Karui?
Are you speaking to me, sir?
Never imagined my people living peacefully with your people, let alone on your lands!
No? Some would say you've been living on Karui islands for generations.
Well, they were our islands by then, weren't they? Anyway, perhaps I should thank you.
Though our beautiful metropolis is now but smoldering ruins, you have given us a new home. A chance to build society anew. Hope.
I didn't do any of that, sir.
You know what I mean! Learn to accept a compliment.

I'm sorry, sir. Allow me to return a compliment: Thank you for not trampling our homes, taking our children, our brothers and sisters, our wives and husbands, and binding their arms and legs when you washed ashore. Thank you for limiting your recolonisation to one island, and for breaking only a few of our laws and traditions in these early days.
You're very welcome. See? It's not hard.
Little fishies told me it's a little bit like this.
Got a few contracts on offer.
Have some contracts, if you need one.

Hey good lookin'. Huh. Most people recognise me. I'm Gianna. Worked a spell in the Chitus Theatre, back when you could leave your house without being followed by Templar secret police. I was Shavronne in <italic>{An Axiom Tragedy}. I played Dialla, the Gemling Queen, in <italic>{Purity Tales}, and the fair lady Merveil in <italic>{Daresso and Merveil}, for which I was very nearly nominated to receive a 'Tario. \r\n\r\nNo? Not a fan of the theatre, I suppose? That's-... That's fine. That act of my story has drawn to a close anyway, but I'm always looking for the next great role. Nothing's quite so thrilling as immersing oneself among the people, and seeing if you can, in fact, pass for the real deal.

I wasn't exactly planning on a life of crime. Yes, most in my profession do end up begging or stealing, but my career was on the up and up, until I was accused of <italic>{Pecuniary Lust} and exiled.

It just so happens that the Boss, cultural elite that he is, saw me in a few shows. He must have noticed my ability to fully embody any role, to become not just the character, but the person. I'm told he was a practitioner of the performing arts himself, in his youth. Obviously, he has a keen eye for talent. 

I'm dying to perform a dialogue with him. Good material is hard to come by 'round here, but I did find a piece by a Bestel floating in the foam. Not particularly engaging, and a frankly unhealthy focus on the female lead's figure in the stage direction, but it's something, at least.

Alas, Kurai maintains the Boss' schedule, and I'm told he is booked up indefinitely. Imagine having lucrative work for months to come! A performer can only dream...

Just my luck! Of course you are put on my contract. Do you even know anything about the theatre? The cursed play? The one no performer should ever name, lest they end up consumed by the phantom that haunts it?

It's said that the play's author wrote it while high as an eagle on ergot. He didn't know, of course, and died upon penning the final word. 

The play, whose name I shall not utter, is about a beautiful young lady who finds herself swept into a world beneath the sands of the Vastiri, where the dead have built a city of bones. She marries a statue, becomes the queen of this city, and then her skin peels off and a hundred little versions of her spill out. Completely nutty. 

It's locked up with the rest of the works deemed distasteful by the Templar, and I simply must have it.

<italic>{Marilla turns to her beloved's unmoving face and speaks the blessed words:

Marilla: Two into one, one into many, to churn the world beneath the crashing dunes. 

Marilla's body shatters like porcelain, each fragment becoming Marilla. Each new Marilla shatters again, and again, each fragment becomes whole. The stage is flooded by Marilla. All is Marilla. The statue rises and exits stage right. 

Fin.}

Wow. I mean... wow. That was something! Right? That... that was something, right? 

I think I might just stick to the unbanned works for a little while, actually. Thanks, though.

You're handling my contract again? I thought I specifically requested someone with a working understanding of the arts! Fine, fine. It's just a job. Well, I'm sure you've done the necessary reading, but I'm dying to gab a bit. 

When I worked with the Theopolis Thespian Society, there was an old, old, <italic>{old} woman. I mean, at <italic>{least} forty. She was our seamstress. She created these costumes that looked just like the real thing. Blackguard uniforms, Templar outfits, you name it. Well, one day she vanished, but the costumes remained. 

I want to get ahold of that old woman's costumes. They were just so... believable! With those, it'll be much easier to slip into a role undetected.

I don't know how she did it. Each outfit so perfectly matches the original piece. It's almost as if-...what!? <italic>{Property of Templar Logistics Office}!? They're the genuine article! That woman stole real bloody uniforms! Well, I guess that explains why they always looked so genuine. It also explains why we didn't ever see her again. \r\n\r\nOh well, her loss is our gain!
Gianna! Yes! And she's a... erm...
A performer actress! Right! And... ehhh...
We met when Vinderi was hired to do the pyrotechnics for a production. He set the curtains on fire, but no one died. I'm here to help you with this job. And other jobs, later. If you want.
Exactly! Anything you'd like to add Gianna?
I think that covers it. Thanks, Vin.
I know set dressing when I see it.
Something about this doesn't ring true... Hmm.
It'd be easier to see with proper stage lighting...
All that time squinting at cue cards has trained me for this.
Back in line, soldier! I will inspect!
Did I say you could speak? Let me do this.
Quiet. ... See? Nothing. I'll show you.
Are you drunk, soldier?! There's nothing on the other side.
Stay in formation! This is a drill!
Obey your orders! I'll take point!
I didn't hear nothin', but let's see.
Oi, keep it down. Gettin' each other spooked. Here, I'll prove it.
Don't be so paranoid. Look, nothing's here...
You're just drunk, mate. Watch, it'll be empty.
Probably just the rats. Afraid of rats? Let's find out!
Nah, you're just losin' it. How could anything be here?
Ease off the elixir. Nothing is here. Observe.
The fumes are affecting your judgement. I shall prove it.
Likely a mere apparition, but I'll make sure.
Perhaps you should rest. I'll check for you.
A hallucinatory phenomena. Anything you see is, as well.
Hearing things is a known side effect, but just to be sure...
Just like the stagehands taught me.
Not the sort of catwalk I thought I'd be walking...
We used one of these backstage, 'til it took a lad's head off.
I need to finish this first.
You can't rush a good performance.
Hey, you're hindering a great performance.
We're just looking around, I swear!
Saw that ending coming a mile away.
That gives me an idea for a character.
You've a keen eye for pretty little things, don't you?
Shh. We don't want an audience.
Keep it down. There's a lot left to do.
Quiet, or we'll have to end early.
This is far more tense than I like.
So much for the plan! Run!
That's not good! We need to rush!
And there, before her, was everything she wanted...
They were so close, they could almost taste it.
In most plays, this is where I'd double-cross you. ... I-... I'm not going to double-cross you.
This is what we're here for. Go on.
Well? Don't keep the audience waiting!
This is the part where you would double-cross me. Please don't.
Now all that's left is to head for the exit.
That's a relief. I always expect a trap for some reason.
People have strange taste, don't you think?
Ladies and gentlemen, the show's about to begin.
Stay on script and hit your marks.
Take a deep breath before we head in. Might be your last.
Focus. Watch your breath and move with caution.
Take your time. This is just the warmup act.
Take a BOW! That was phenomenal!
How about a bloody round of applause, eh?
By Innocence, I do love a happy ending.
Faultless! Stunning! An incredible performance! And you were also very good!
I know there's something wrong here, just need a bit of time!
A lot of work went into hiding something here!
Some convincing fakes here! What are they hiding!?
Open it! Let them through! Oh, I'll do it!
Stand back! I'll take them on single handedly!
Make way! I must let the reinforcements in!
Give passage! I have a plan!
I'll open the passage, and you take them alive!
Wait, ain't they with us!? They is, right!?
Can't get 'em from this side! Pop 'er open!
If we let 'em through, they'll be too confused to fight!
Oi, boss wants us to open the door!
I ain't scared, mate! I'm opening it!
Allow passage! We shall claim their ichors!
They beg to be sacrificed! I say we let them!
Their flesh demands passage! We must obey!
We must unify! Open the gate!
Separation is trickery! Open the way!
They test our faith! Let faith shield you!
We've got to get across as soon as it's ready!
This sort of thing always breaks when everyone's watching!
I can play a thousand roles, but not at once!
Can you see I'm in the middle of something!?
Do something or this will take forever!
Let us through, or face your death!
It's like they forget they're the villains! Wait... Are they the villains? No, yeah, they're the villains.
Make sure that's not a posthumous award!
Great find, but shouldn't we be leaving!?
Don't be blinded by all that glitters!
Wrap it up! I don't want this to be my final role!
Get it! I can't handle the suspense!
It's there! Grab it while we can!
We're so close! The tension is palpable!
Good! Now rush to the exit!
Hope you're not waiting for applause!
Vinderi, ever thought about a keg that makes a lot of smoke but no explosion?
Lass, that might be the stupidest idea I've ever heard.
They say all the world's a stage...
And no one gets a happy ending. Yes?
Speaking of, would you care to accompany on a date, Gianna?
Niles! I said save it for later!
What an horrible, horrible thing to say.
What happened to that little basement theatre where we first met, Gianna?
Oh, the Wilted Quill? Yeah, burnt down.
All mortal endeavour is sand cast to the winds.
Yeah, but, acting... that endures. People care about good acting. The universe cares about good acting.
If harm comes to you, Gianna, I will hold myself responsible.
Good, I was planning to hold you responsible too.
Don't want to hear no complaints. We all signed up for this.
Actually, I auditioned! ... and I got the role.
Please no, my bloody knees are giving me trouble.
A performance worthy of an audience! Do they have plays where you're from Nenet?
No. All the battles are very real.
By surviving. The dead feel great boredom.
That went so well I could kiss someone!
Oh, but Niles, what if I accidentally turn you into a prince? I sure would miss you.
Did you see me in there? Damn, I'm good.
Yes, I did see you, which is very much the opposite of what we wanted. You got lucky.
Worthy of a grand play, eh Gianna?
Honestly? That went too smoothly. If one of us had died, that would have been dramatic!
That was a... five thumb performance, yes?
Five stars. The thumbs are a different thing.
At last. So how about that Date, Gianna?
(<italic>{Laughs}) I can't remember the last time I laughed that hard! Thanks Niles!
Gianna, you nearly bloody blew it for us.
You need to keep a lower bloody profile.
Say, before we get too deep into this, do you think my role could use an accent?
Well, it depends quite a lot on--
Oh! What about a limp? Or an eyepatch!
That might draw too much att--
I'm Big Toe Gren, Captain of the Salty Hound.
... Good. Well, now I know we have that to fall back on.
Already? I thought we had at least a few weeks! What do we do?! WHAT DO WE DO!?
No, no! Vin! Me! I mean me!
What did you think was happening?
Nothing! Nothing! Just... if a living flame asks after me, I'm not here.
Hello all! Did I miss anything important?
Oh. Can you catch me up?
I can. We have a job. You have a role to play.
Well, uh, thank you Nenet. Very concise.
Wonderful. Just wonderful. And yourself? Wait, no, let me try to guess. I see... shoes. Boots. Steel toed. You wish to go hiking.
They're striking... some trousers. Black. Right in the in-seam. Over and over.
Yes. A vivid imagination. Just wonderful.
Your armour is looking sooo shiny today Huck.
Can't wait to see what's underneath.
Okay Gi, give it a rest. We have work to do.
Thanks, lady Kurai. Good role for me today?
That, I suspect, is up to you.
We still have a little more planning to do, but I hope you'll find whatever role you are given fulfilling.
Whoops, must've taken a wrong turn.
No, wait, you're meant to be here. We're planning a heist!
Well that's lucky! I'd just cancelled my plans for the rest of the day.
Oh, just the usual armour. Helps protect the ol' bones.
No, I mean, what were you doing later today?
I'm afraid I'm busy, dear. Got a heist to plan. Very flattered though.
Nenet! Mind if I practise your accent?
Actually, I think I do mind.
Eckchully, I tink I do mind.
I'm needed? Oh, lady Gianna, what an incomparable pleasure.
My Oriathan rose, my shimmering jewel among the rhoa dung.
Ha. Really, what are my orders.
Gi, I think we need to focus.

Hm? Ah! Right, Ahem. Vinderi. Pleasure to meet your acquaintance. Err, pleased to make you. Hello. \r\n\r\nName's Vinderi. Did I mention that already? No one alive knows as much about the explosive arts as me. If you want something or someone, or several someones, turned into an unrecognisable, smouldering mess, I'm more than happy to oblige.

I was walking around the catacombs beneath the square, trying to find my way to the sewers under the courts. Had a huge sack of the blue stuff on my back. Leaving a little trail as I go so I can find my way out. Little azurite fuse trail winding its way back to the storehouse. Cost me an arm and a leg, that powder. Anyway, I'm right under where I thought the High Templar's office was. Start piling the powder up right under his fat arse. Planning to blow him back to Innocence. 

Well, I start hearing a hissing noise. And I start seeing the blue light down the end of the tunnel turning an angry red. It's moving towards me quick. And I'm thinking, this is it. This is where it ends for me, but at least I'll blow that high pain in the arse skyward. Then it stops. No hissing. No light. Just a silhouette. Tall as a man ever was. Taller than Tibbs. Don't know how he even got through the storehouse hole. This man... this glorious man! 

Put it down! He shouts. It's not worth the trouble. Come. It's time to go! So I put the bag down, and I start walking over to him. Running even. This man saved my life. I swear to myself I'll follow this Eternal Ideal of a man, this statue, this perfect specimen, as far as he will have me. And as I get close, my eyes adjust. This beautiful man comes into focus. His hand is extended to meet me. I reach out mine. There's an electricity between us. And as my fingers lock into his, he slaps a manacle around my wrist. I'm under arrest for attempted deicide and possession of a dangerous substance. Got me exiled, the pig. Once I got here I just started working for the boss.

What was your question?
Niko? Niko... Was he the lad with the club foot? No, wait, Niko was the haberdasher. The bordello owner? No?

Niko... ah! Of course! The miner boy. That's miner, not, er, minor. I do believe he was of age when last I saw him. Strange lad. Always felt like he was talking at me, not to me, if you follow. Had an awful lot of yellow powder for sale. Wonder what ever happened to him? Lost track of many in that line of work. A shame, but not a surprise.

You've got a contract you want me to take a look at? Alright, why not.

Mmhm. Mmm. Yes. Well, everything seems to be in order. 

...

...Oh! This was mine! Well, the designs have changed a bit, but the fundamentals are the same. It's a grocery list, except instead of the markets, we're going to an alchemy storehouse I'm not supposed to know exists. And instead of groceries, we're going to collect a number of powders, ichors and minerals I'm running low on. And instead of paying for them, we are going to steal them. So in that sense, it is very unlike a grocery list. Straightforward enough. Ready to go?

...Thirty three cubits of cerulean alloy thread, half an ounce of vitriolic talc, two quarts of bishop-blessed cleansing alcohol -- that's for me -- and enough barrel hoops to sink a bloated bonechewer. Perfect. 

...Wait. Hold on. Hold on one dang minute. Where the--... Where is the fumarole tar? Don't tell me I forgot the fumarole tar! Without the tar I might as well be baking a tray of Keth flatbread.

Oh dear. I didn't even have it on the list. Sorry, Exile, the error is mine. You've earned your markers. Hopefully I'll have enough left to take out another contract.

Hmm? Oh! At last! The Fumarole Tar job! Gods, I've been chomping at the bit for this contract. 

I've drawn up plans for a bomb that, well, let's just say it'll put The Ring on the map. Or take it off the map. It might take quite a large area off the map, actually. 

I tend to deal with controlled explosions, but who doesn't love an uncontrolled explosion? Whoever's nearby, that's who! But other than them, they're great! And this is going to be really, really great.

There's only one place I know of that houses enough Fumarole Tar for the job, and it has all sorts of other experimental goodies that I'd like to get my hands on, too. 

Exile, this thing is really going to set your world on fire. I feel like a child again!

I've finished it, Exile. It's all done! The Vinderi Bomb is complete at last! I've named it after myself. It's my legacy. Or, the ruins it will leave in its wake will be my legacy. I wonder if it works... Shall we try it out?\r\n\r\n We only get one attempt! Let's do it!

Bwaaahahaha! Had you going there for a bit, didn't I? I may be old, but I've still got a little pop left in my powderkeg. Did you really think I was about to blow us all to Innocence? Give this old man a little credit!

I just wanted to give the good folk here a little show. I call these beauties "Explodey-make-good-lookers". Catchy, eh? Reckon there might be a business in it!

Well, I hope you enjoyed it. Consider it a show of gratitude.
Let me go get my things.
Good timing. I've been looking for something to do.
Needed a reason to stretch these old legs.
Got the perfect powder for this job.
Let's pop this little sucker open.
Haven't come across this make before. Well, let's give it a go.
Ooh. Solidly built. Open up to me. It's okay, be vulnerable.
Now, how do I work this thing again?
You don't expect me to jump, do you?
I have the thing for this somewhere...
I did bring the thing. Did I? Thought I did...
I was hoping I wouldn't have to remember how to use this blasted thing
Ah, clever. Not clever enough, but still.
Not the worst trap. Not the best, but not the worst.
Oh, those clever bastards. Hmm. Hmmmmmm.
Easy pe--...oh. Oh no. Oh? Oh.
Huh. Looks like a twist on a Maloney design.
Yes, yes... I have just the thing!
I've been saving this one just for you.
Oh, sure, rush the guy with the bombs.
\"It was all going so well, then Vinderi blew us all up because I got impatient.\"
Pick on someone your own age.
Stop hitting me, you nitwit. I have BOMBS.
Idiot's trying to blow us both up!
I'm old, but you'll still die sooner!
Whew, that gets the ol' heart racing.
That, my friend, is very expensive looking.
In my younger days I'd fight you for that.
Bit of advice: keep that little find to yourself.
We're going to get found out if we're not careful.
When even I think we're too loud, that's a problem.
That noise? That is not a good noise.
I know that sound. That's a bad sound.
Well, go on then. That's what we're here for.
We've made it this far. Why stop now?
Come on, legs, don't fail me now.
Great! ...How do we get out of here again?
How about you get us out of here, huh?
Wait. Powder, sparks, probe aaaand... Yep. We're good.
Even at my age, the quiet before a job gives me goosebumps.
Remember to breathe when we get in. Can't tell you how many good men and women I've lost to forgetting to breathe.
Bit of advice from an old hand: Whatever you do, and this is really, really important,
so listen carefully. Don't, and I repeat, don't, DO NOT, forget to follow this advice. Here it is:
I suggest you listen, because if you listen, you'll really take it on board.
Too many of your generation forget to listen, especially when good advice is being given.
Are you listening? Don't get distracted.
It's easy to hear someone, but listening and hearing are two totally different things. So don't just hear; listen.
What are you looking at me for?
We're on a job. Don't just stare at me. Focus!
Why do they keep taking on these glassy-eyed dimwits.
People ask me why I do this at my age. People are rude.
Oh, me heart! I auugh-- ...Oh, thank the gods. False alarm.
Glad I didn't tell you I nearly blew my arms off during prep!
You are mad, Exile. Mad! And I love it!
What a rush! Can't pay for that kind of experience. Even crazier that we're getting paid to do it!
Hahaha! I'd never've told my kids this, but gods, I love crime. I just love doing a good crime!
\"Vinderi, you're not busy running for your life are you?!\"
You're insane, you know that, right?!
I don't work well under pressure!
How in the--... oh! Found it!
You have the thing!? Wait, I have the thing!
Ah! I've got the thing for this! Here we go--no, that's not it. AH! Here we go!
A gap! I have just the tool for this. Somewhere. Did I drop it? Ha! I was holding it! Don't you just hate that?!
This is meant to be DELICATE work!
The whole place is a damnable death trap!
Wait! This thing's rigged to kill us!
Gods! You were planning to blunder into this thing!
Trap! Trap! Stop! There's a trap! A trap!
This is exactly the sort of thing we should have handled earlier!
Can't even take the time to enjoy this!
If I die, I hope this blows you up too!
Gods, these are NOT ideal conditions for handling explosive materials!
I wanted to save this one for a special occasion. You owe me a new bomb!
I don't have a twin you know! He's long dead!!
Not like this! Not like this!
Help! I'm too young to die!
Why are you still grabbing things!?
Can't use it if you're dead!
Great, now you got more loot than brains!
There it is! What are you waiting for?!
If you don't get it now, you don't get it at all!
Go on then! Make a path!
Found a weird mole this morning. Nenet?
You all know what we're doing, right?
Of course I do you freaky bastard. ...But I'll follow your lead. For safety's sake.
Call out if you need a powderkeg.
Bwaaahahaha! Still funny! So many times, and it's still very, very funny.
The air is sour. Something is ami--
Gods, that stew was too old, wasn't it. Sorry, everyone.
Perhaps we should take mental fortitude into consideration for future expeditions.
Why, you looking for a little time off? Ha!
Oh, I stand by what I said.
Pace yourselves. Exhaustion down there means death.
Gods, you almost make it sound tempting. A nice, long nap.
Did you see that back there?
Even if the gods did exist, which they don't, do you think they would care to hear your dull opines?
Best watch your mouth, interrogator. Got a powderkeg that fits right in it.
Oh, I'd love to see you try.
Got enough loot in there to choke an ex-blackguard in his sleep!
Err, not you. Different guy. Goes by, uh, Buck.
Victory, and yet the buzzards circle.
Oh, they're here for me. Buzz off! Blasted birds. I'm not dead yet!
Humanity triumphs where the divine dare not tread.
Better than I hoped. Much better than I feared.
Honestly, thought you'd blow us up.
Kurai! Just the lady I was looking for.
Oh? I was just about to look for you!
Looking for a reason to destroy Niles?
No, but it sounds like you might be.
Not at all, no, nothing of the sort. Got plenty of reasons! Just looking for permission.
Well, can I ask the Boss?
The scale of the bomb... where are we supposed to get all the powder?
It's a building, not a bomb.
Let us put our differences aside. The job comes first.
Vinderi, been meaning to ask you. Where'd you come up with the powder mixes?
Trying to make me obsolete, are ya?
Gonna run back to Dominus with my precious formulas!? I know your game.
Forget it, Vin. Just making small-talk.
Vinderi, thank you for joining us.
Not a problem. What do you need from me?
We're hoping you can help us on a job.
Is she? Where's she hiding? Help me look... erm...
Yes, help me look for Nenet, erm... uhh...
Ah! There she is. Thank you, uh, you.
Hello, hello. Ah. I see you'll employ absolutely any rabble.
You know it was. I know you know it was.
Keep your greasy little head out of mine, or else.
...good... GOD... What--...No! Vile! What monster pictures such a thing.
I did warn you. I did warn him.
A bloody big stupid head! Boom!
Oh, come on. He was asking for it.
S'fine. Just focus on the job, yeah?
Exile, this is Vinderi. Expert demolitionist.
Nice to meet you, Vinderi. My name's Vinderi too! Isn't that funny?
Years of exposure to fumes has... affected him.
Sorry to hear that. Luckily I'm fiddle as a fit!

You are an exile? Then you, too, have had your rightful home stolen from you - unless you actually committed the crimes you were accused of.\r\n\r\nBut of course you haven't. We are all innocent here, yes?

I have been looking for someone to follow my entire life. Someone to inspire me, to give meaning and community to my days. The Boss is... to put it bluntly, not that man. However, he is better than nothing.\r\n\r\nBecause of what he has built here, we unwanted scum have what some could call a society. Here, everyone is welcome regardless of station or ability, provided they are willing to work. The Boss has made it so.

I am honoured, Exile, that one of your strength would even speak to me, let alone help me. I am an outcast, and it is that very status which drives me for this mission. I have traveled far, and for many years, to find the resources and allies to do what I intend. Here I am in this place, before you now, ready.

Where I am from, the Plains of Vastiri, the Maraketh hold no pity for the weak or the supposedly useless. The other outcasts found me and raised me, and though our lives are harsh, we have a meager culture of our own. We call ourselves the Faridun. The Maraketh believe we are worthless and flawed, but I am convinced I can prove that is not true.

There is a legend among my people of a bold warrior who tried to unite the scattered Faridun camps thousands of years ago. His name was Jamanra, and he wished only to unify us so that we might come into our own as a people. If I can prove that he existed by finding the Book of Jamanra, then I may be able to initiate a ritual challenge with the Maraketh to test Faridun warriors for worthiness. If we pass, they will have to accept us back into the lives we should have had! Will you help me win back my home, Exile?

Jamanra did exist, Exile... and they killed him. The Sekhemas agreed to meet with him to discuss recognizing the Faridun nation, but it was a trick. They poisoned him. The supposedly honourable high-and-mighty Maraketh poisoned our greatest leader.\r\n\r\nI suppose I should have expected nothing less from this brutal world we live in, Exile. You and I know best that hope is an illusion, and that raw force is the only way to take anything for oneself. In any case, I thank you for aiding me.

I have come to a decision, Exile. I do not believe the Maraketh will ever willingly give us a home, or let us make our own. The Book you helped me retrieve tells Jamanra's tale, but it goes a bit further than that. It also tells of his final resting place. You can already guess what I intend, yes? In this land of madness where the dead rise and legendary figures return, I have a reasonable suspicion Jamanra can be found and released from his tomb.

If the Maraketh will not listen to our peaceful pleas, then perhaps we Faridun will carve a home for ourselves on the Plains of Vastiri with the sharp edge of a sword. Jamanra can finish what he began thousands of years ago, and if he is empowered by Corruption this time around, then no cowardly poison will be able to stop him.

Help me find Jamanra in his tomb and convince him to lead our cause, Exile!

Jamanra was a raving mad monster... there is no hope, Exile. I appreciate your aid, but I no longer see a way forward. Who was I to think that I could change thousands of years of brutal tradition? This life of thievery and villainy is all that there is for me.\r\n\r\nI think I'm going to take refuge in mead from now on.

Although Isla is often distracted, she is quite kind. She has a strength I have never seen before, one born of machines and intellect rather than fighting skill. I would never admit this to anyone, of course, but her steadfast support makes this place almost feel like a home. That is, when her mechanical spider isn't chewing my belongings.

It is an elegant lie, that name: the 'Plains' of Vastiri. I know it only as a harsh desert, a blasted wasteland of broken rock, crimson sands, and salted earth. Those who call it the 'Plains' see it as it was thousands of years ago. They are deluded.\r\n\r\nBut who am I to judge? I still believe I'll find a home someday, even with a face like mine. Perhaps we all need a few delusions to keep us sane. What's your flavour of madness, Exile?

Sometimes, when you are near, I hear whispers. Even though I have the best ears among all these thieves, I cannot make out the words... but they sound like my constant companions - my depression, paranoia, and hatred - when I am at my worst. Be careful, Exile.
Your orders shall be my law.
I will not fail the group.
You will not regret including me.
Allow me a moment to focus...
Seeing sometimes relies on more than one's eyes.
They might as well have left this unlocked.
Did they even try to secure this?
I can break this vault. No problem.
I'll be with you in a moment.
I hear you, but cannot yet.
Fight together and we shall overcome!
Today is not the end, then.
I knew we could do it.
Take what you can. Live for now.
I hope you will share that.
Should we really delay like this?
We can ill afford any more mistakes.
They will catch on to our presence.
Do you remember what to do?
If you need help, I am here.
Nenet, good to have you here.
Then I will do my best to serve!
Yes, we'll need your skills for this one.
I will not let you down.
Hah, I'm no Captain, but I appreciate it.
You better be. This is going to be a tough one.
Just tell me what to do!
Out of curiosity, pariah, do the Faridun worship any gods?
Niles, I can feel you trying to read my thoughts.
Oh bleak one, when a man believes he is doomed, he usually finds a way to make it happen.
Good thing for you that I am not a man.
Perhaps this is the day that we shall die.
In your mythology, what happens to the Faridun after death?
I shall likely let you know soon.
Like the ribcage of a dunewalker as the buzzards pick out his organs.
Where we go, death follows swiftly.
How come you and I never just talk?
Oh! Want to exchange bleak tales of oppression after this?
This was a doomed run, yet we cheated fate.
There is no fate but what we make!
Gods, I feel immortal! What a rush.
Be glad that you are not. Immortality dulls the senses. To be mortal is to feel all life has to offer.
Death's pursuit is inescapable, but we have delayed it this day.
Reckon that calls for a celebration!
I'll crack their minds like so many rhoa eggs.
I can almost hear their thoughts...
Isla says the mind is just another system of gears...
Thank you for letting me participate.
I will not let you down.
I just want to be useful.
We will survive this. I trust.
I knew we would make it.
Let's return to that rat-ridden place we call home.
I hope the Boss approves of my performance.
My prediction of our deaths appears to have been wrong.

Sir! Sorry, old habit. You'll get used to it. Blackguard training did a number on me. I'm Huck. Served in the Oriath 3rd for five years. Dishonourably discharged, though I consider that an honour. 

My time with the Blackguards put a lot of things in perspective, least once I had some distance from them. What we do here might be illegal, but that don't make it wrong. 

You need something -- anything -- you come to me, yeah? We're family now. Family look out for each other.

Haven't actually met him myself. Been dealing mostly with lady Kurai. Bit like the old days, really. Orders come down the chain and stop when they hit the right pair of ears.\r\n\r\nI'm eager to meet him though. Owe him my life. Had some very dark days after I got discharged. Not a lot of people want to hire veterans, especially when they leave the service under less-than-ideal circumstances. But the Boss secured me a place to live, and gave me a steady income and work to keep me busy.

Ah, my contract. Took it out not long after joining the Ring to track down a mate of mine. Man named Enoch. Not easy making friends at my age, but active duty has a way of forging near-unbreakable bonds. Enoch and I got real close. Might as well've been brothers. Right before I got discharged, Enoch was called up to a special unit we'd heard rumours about. A group under the direction of Piety, of all people. Supposedly some elite strike force, but no one personally knew anyone who was a part of it. 'Til Enoch, that is. \r\n\r\nAfter I started working for the Boss, I asked Whakano to find Enoch. Thought he might be a good fit. But Whakano found no traces. I want to break into the Blackguard Records and find out where he's deployed.
Let's see... Good. Enoch's file is in here. Let's go.

Gods damn them. Piety, Dominus, Gravicius, the whole lot of 'em. They moved Enoch into an 'Unspecified Research' unit.
