Some may call me a traitor, but I do not seek the destruction of my brethren. I seek their salvation.

I know what Jamanra intends, for the Maraketh have made a grave error. Atop their burial spires lie their most honoured dead. Our new Queen demanded he seek any trace of ancient flesh from those of renown or power in life. <continue>He intends to feed their bodies to a horrific creature he keeps in a cage behind his throne. They call it the Beast. I have seen it, and the sight haunts my nightmares...
We have met in battle, but not in peace. I am Balbala, once a traitor, long a sorrowed prisoner. <continue>As Djinn, here I shall serve as your guide. Together, we shall prove ourselves worthy.

You have danced with death... and survived. The trial is complete! <continue>Whether they like it or not, the others must accept you as a dekhara now. The tale-woman life was never meant for you. I can see that, so perhaps they will come to see it as well. <continue>I will remain here for the time being. I am finally free, but I find I do not wish to rest just yet. <continue>This place is in disrepair. Though it may take another thousand years, I must restore it to its former glory. Should you need me, I will continue to serve as your guide here.

It is done! You are no longer a jingakh! You now carry with you the spirit of a Maraketh dekhara. <continue>I am finally free, but I find I do not wish to rest just yet. <continue>This place is in disrepair. Though it may take another thousand years, I must restore it to its former glory. <continue>Should you need me, I will continue to serve as your guide here.

I have had a great many years to think on my foolish choices, and now all I want is to earn my right to rest. <continue>This place was built to determine honour, to prove oneself worthy as a Sekhema. Tradition allowed for one dekhara, and one advisor. <continue>If I aid you here, and if you succeed, then my crimes will finally be forgiven. Then, and only then, may I join those that have gone before.

I hardly know the woman I was before. I remember betraying my akhara, but the reasons why now feel petty and small. <continue>If I could go back, if I could speak to the woman I was, I would tell her what a fool she was being. Would she listen? Probably not... <continue>The mistakes we make are shaped from who we are.

The tale-women of many akharas gathered on the day of my sentencing. Death was not punishment enough for my crime. <continue>They enacted the ritual, but my imprisonment as Djinn would not have been possible without my willful agreement. <continue>I accepted. I let it happen, because I deserved it. <continue>I have no idea how long I was trapped there, but it was as close to eternity as I can possibly imagine.
The role of advisor is strictly bound by tradition. I may offer you aid, but only in certain specific ways. <continue>Look to me in your times of doubt.

The river inside you, the essence of who you are, can be torn out of you under the right conditions. It can be speared, or bottled, or chained. <continue>A spirit without a body, especially one created in this manner, is called a Djinn. It has prolonged my existence, but it is not a form anyone should desire... <continue>I grow hungry, but cannot eat. I grow tired, but cannot sleep. I would give anything just to feel the chill of a single sip of water one more time.

What happened to the Plains of Vastiri? The land has changed so much since the time of my imprisonment. <continue>There were several desert regions slowly spreading, but it wasn't like this. <continue>The very Gates where I committed my crimes were water-locks for a river. Now, there is nothing but sand and salt flats. <continue>How could they have allowed this to happen?
If you wish to challenge the Trial again, find more baryas, more coins. <continue>The Djinn within will inhabit this place, much like I do.
The foe ahead is... Formidable. Steel yourself.
Two ancient guardians await you ahead.
This was the end of the Trial in my time... But I sense another being resides here. Perhaps you can challenge them, if you can find them.
This battle is our sacred duty.
I understand now. Perhaps my purpose was to be here, to aid you in this, all along. Thank you.
You have failed, but you will have another chance.
Death is different here. You will have another chance.
I would give anything for a sip.
Let the river be your path.
Let the river be your path.
I remember when this was new...
I remember when this was new...
I am older than that artefact...
I am older than that artefact...
You need more Sacred Water for that.
You need more Sacred Water for that.
As you progress through the trial, collect the Sacred Water you find. Bring it to me and I will be able to assist you further.
And so it begins... A true test of your mettle! Ready yourself!
Victory is found one move at a time!
Can that really be him? I recognise his voice.
They ripped out his soul, like they did to me, but he refused to be imprisoned.
We cannot allow him to disgrace this sacred place!
I know you can defeat him.
I wish I could do more.
I wish I could do more.
I'll try to be of more help.
I'll try to be of more help.
We will deliver you to Traitor's Passage, which will allow you to ascend the cliffs.

Ah yes, <italic>{jingakh}, I hear you are interested in Keth. If we are to travel there, I would like you to attempt to do something for us. As a girl, before I danced with the scorpion, my favourite tale was that of a spirit that dances in the ruins of Keth. The last djinn, the third servant of water, bearing the name Amnaah. A minor power, one a mortal could reasonably hope to best.\r\n\r\nI have long held hope that this tale is true - that all my tales are true. Capturing it would serve as proof that these stories I hold in my head and pass on to the younger generation are more than simply myths. Over the years, I have kept an eye out for artifacts that might hold such a being. I believe this bottle may serve. Will you take it and capture Amnaah? You would make a young girl very happy, even though she is quite old now.
Before we travel to the dunes over Keth, Zarka wishes to speak with you.

Once the seat of power for our people, now a buried testament to a glorious past. We will build a new Keth someday, when all this is over, and the Maraketh people will shine under the sun once again. That is a promise.

It is our bane, young one. The desert is a harsh Sekhema. It is not the heat that kills you, nor the thirst, nor the chill winds at night. The Doom of the Desert is a severing of one's connection to other people. <continue>The desert is always shifting, and one rock looks much like another. Those who lose hold of their path for even a moment are never seen again, and those who fall among the dunes are forgotten, their bodies lost beneath the sands for all time. <continue>As a girl, I sometimes had nightmares about a layer beneath... a layer of bones... countless generations of Maraketh that have fallen from memory... being forgotten under the sands is our deepest fear, too unnerving for many to discuss, and it is why a promise to remember someone is the greatest respect we children of the desert can give.

Foreigners often misunderstand the concept of Sekhema. I am no dictator, and do not make some pathetic claim of divine right. <continue>Emperors are for nations filled with the weak-minded and soft, as history has proven every time an empire falls and we endure. <continue>I am Sekhema because others have put their faith in me as the strongest and most capable among us. I lead because there is no better replacement. It is a role I deserve, by definition.
You need not trust me. You will see the truth of my information soon enough. I ask nothing of you, only that you do what you know is right.
What is that being? Does it travel with you? I would tell you not to trust a mysterious stranger in black, but that would make my own situation rather difficult...

I cannot say I view the Maraketh favourably, but there is no other power to which I can turn. Jamanra is going mad, and I know that the Maraketh will unite their scattered akharas to confront him if the need is great enough. I believe that it is.

Meeting the Ardura is disconcerting. Like most Faridun, I was left to die in the desert as an infant. Perhaps someone here is my mother or father... <continue>I look at each of them wondering what my life could have been if... if they had wanted me. My people are full of anger and distrust, for reasons I hope are clear. They are blinded by this.

The weary traveler grows close to the end of the path! The breadbowl of the world, the verdant Land of Seven Waters, awaits! Be sure to have your toll ready at the Gates. Cloth, gems, metal wares, and coin are all accepted.

The traitor Balbala has been sentenced to one thousand years of suffering as a djinn, bound in this place of her dishonour. Let no woman or man of Maraketh blood enter her prison before her time is served.

The weary traveler has reached the end of the path! Welcome to the City of Seven Waters, whence bounty springs! Behold our lush plains and verdant forests, blessed to feed empires far and wide. Eat, drink, and be fat at your leisure, so long as you take word back to your homeland of the glory of Keth!
Let these towers stand for all time, so that the sands may never swallow the Honoured Dead. We give you to the sky and to the wind, in defiance of the Doom of the Desert.
You must get out. The mouth closed after we touched the rare blue vein of ore, and something lurking in the dark now stalks us... something enormous...

Winter deepens, bringing a biting chill. I long for it to snow, for the wonder I felt as a child to grace my eyes once more, but the last winter that brought such beauty was two hundred years ago now... it cannot snow in a region where it does not rain. 

The city is quiet. The city is cold. The wind whistles through stone columns, unheard by the living. I ask myself why I am still here. I ask myself why I will not let my tired bones rest, and I ask myself whether I truly believe Halani will awaken.

I do.

I do...

The spirits... they move... they rise. Unhallowed things from the nightmares of the Mastodons use their graves to enter our world. We trap them in the bones... we dance, we sing, we live. A testament to chained evil.

Why would you show me this? You fool! This folly is only harmless because there are no names on this letter. Otherwise, tradition would demand unhappy duties of me. I value each and every one of my <italic>{dekhara}. This is why I say: get this out of my sight.

Ah. I see. You would do well, child, not to show that letter to any other pair of eyes. If I am asked about its contents, I shall feign dementia. <continue>I suggest you... dispose of it... by giving it to someone who cannot read it. Am I being clear?

Nasima, yes, Nasima! A great warrior, though with a complicated legacy. Born with eyes the color of blood, she was left to die among the dunes for being blind, but the Faridun found her and raised her. <continue>A <italic>{balbalakh}, one might think, but no. She became an impressive warrior in her own right, and when called upon to raid her people, she recognised her mother's voice, and turned and slaughtered her Faridun captors! <continue>A true role model from the ancient days, and a wonderful sleep-tale for the children.
Well done! Come in and speak with the others.
Well, sir... We have arrived. The Vastiri awaits. Good luck to you.
Well, my lady... We have arrived. The Vastiri awaits. Good luck to you.
<italic>{It appears someone rode in on this rhoa, but never left...}
Did Zarka send you, outsider? Then let us do battle!
Advance with me! There are two more gates we must open!
The Faridun have never organized in such numbers before. They fight as if they no longer fear death.
If we can allow the caravan through all three gates, my warriors will swarm them under.
Let us find the figurehead of this horde!
This final gate must be opened from the watchtower ahead.
The Maraketh do not bow to kings. We skin them.
Make haste! He must not escape!
The pretender king has escaped, for now. Let us return to the caravan and question this defector.
Foreigner, time is of the essence!
Doing a Sekhema's dirty work, foreigner?
We will finish this, but not today.

I must pursue what I feel to be right. Asala might yet decide to have me put to death, or abandon me to the Doom of the Desert. I knew these risks, but I had to try anyway. <continue>If you had seen the darkness rising in the hearts of my brothers and sisters, you would understand. I am not betraying them. I am trying to save them from themselves.

I have given all the help I can. The rest will be up to you and the Ardura. I have no doubt Asala will lead all of you to victory. <continue>I would wish you a swift triumph, but I know my maddened brothers and sisters will fight like rabid animals. Do what you must.
Somehow, she knows when I am near. She frowns and turns away. I fear no one here will ever accept me, but I cannot go back to my people now.

Now that she is willing to talk to me, I find that Shambrin is very kind. I think she understands what it is to be an outsider. If she had been born blind, she would have been a sister-outcast among the Faridun. Being blinded as a warrior, however, guarantees her place among her people. <continue>Had I been an Ardura warrior whose lungs became weakened by sickness rather than birth, I would have been her sister here. I think about that life sometimes.

The Maraketh have no idea how great we number. We are larger than any one akhara by far, and my brothers and sisters held a great bitterness even before Corruption came among us. <continue>Everything we do, from our garb to our food, is made opposite to the Maraketh out of spite. I still feel some of that anger when I see them here, standing proud and colourful. <continue>Asala promises them a return to their glory days, but do they not have such glory now?
She is the only one willing to talk with me. I could listen to her stories for days. She truly does not seem to care that I am not of the Ardura...

My life would have been much better if I had known someone like Zarka growing up. She cares about everyone here, no matter their station.  <continue>She has even told me that if I prove myself, I might be accepted here someday. I think that is something I want.

This Corruption that plagues the land. I cannot bring myself to fully believe it is the reason for my people's sickening turn. I know that when the Beast first came to us—when Jamanra was raised from death—he quickly became covetous and prone to fits of rage.  <continue>Soon, that fervor gleamed in the eyes of those around him. You say it is Corruption, but I have not seen anything in my brothers and sisters that was not already there. Corruption may exist, yes, but it does not fully control. It only... excuses. <continue>The Faridun are warring against the Maraketh because they desire to do so. They have always wanted this conflict. They want to make those who abandoned us suffer.

The Maraketh abandoned us, but there is beauty in their strict traditions. They do not have a choice. The desert is a harsh Sekhema, as they say. <continue>Uniting as one people, combining our resources - that is the only way we can all live in peace.

We Faridun have never had grand caravans. In our preparations, Jamanra tasked our people with building one of our own. The intent shifted as madness crept upon him.  <continue>Soon, it became the greatest war machine the Vastiri has ever known. The wish for a better life was gone. Only thoughts of hatred were left.

This... Oriana... the one you called a 'Countess'... Jamanra has declared her our Queen. She first came to us from the south, and seemed sympathetic to our cause. She promised us power... the power to take back our lives. <continue>She left for Ezomyte lands, vowing to return with something that would resurrect our greatest hero, Jamanra. With that hope dangled before us, the Faridun united for the first time since his death. We prepared, as she asked. We took the quarry. We began working on the Dreadnought. <continue>I am ashamed to admit I was a devout believer in the cause... until the day she kept her promise. She did return. She did bring the power to resurrect Jamanra. She brought... the Beast.

The sight of that thing chilled my soul. Those of us who objected to its presence were forced to work, mining and finishing the Dreadnought. <continue>By the time we were done, madness was already rife, and we were sealed in the mine to die for supposedly betraying our people...
I will tell your tale, <italic>{jingakh}. Return someday, and you might hear Risu tell it in my place.
Each young one is much like another. Faridun, Maraketh, what does it matter to an old woman? Others may scowl for letting Risu sit and listen to my stories, but none may order me silent.

She was a fierce warrior before she was blinded in battle. Focused, determined. Losing her sight has not changed that. I have no doubt that she will become skilled enough at blind-fighting to rejoin the ranks someday. Indeed, blind <italic>{dekhara} were once instrumental in decimating an Eternal legion during a sandstorm ambush, so it is not without precedent.
Trust in her, <italic>{jingakh}. While you are here, she is your Sekhema, and she will not lead you astray.
If her information proves to be truthful, then she will live. If she is a deceiver sent to misdirect us, she will be left to die in the open desert... <i>{again}.
The <italic>{balbalakh} has her life, for she was truthful. If she also wishes to be accepted here, that will be up to her.

She is a devoted follower, and there is no difference now between Maraketh and Faridun. Both serve me, under my united banner. The glory days of our people are nigh, <italic>{jingakh}. If you wish, you may return once you have destroyed the Seed of Corruption, and you, too, may share in what we build.

I am loathe to allow you access to the sacred burial towers of our people, but better a single <italic>{jingakh} than an army of spiteful enemies. The towers must be protected, no matter the cost. They are part of our legacy. We will defend their outskirts while you ascend and undertake your grisly duty.
You left a child to die. He holds a new loyalty now.
Then why did you never come look for me after your ascension?
I did die, after thirty years living among the Faridun. It was a harsh life filled with pain, and I hated you every moment of it.
No. Save your breath for when my King arrives and lets the Seed feast upon your flesh.
I believed my hate would subside seeing you eaten alive, but I am still empty.
There is nothing left for me but hate... and slaying Maraketh.
You sided with the villains, fool.
So our Honoured Dead have been destroyed. Better this fate than letting a foul creature of Corruption consume them. Do not speak of this, lest our <italic>{dekharas} fear for their places of honour.
We have their trail now. They will not escape!

We have spent our time wisely. The journey so far has cost us several weeks, but our most distant outriders have managed to distract the Faridun with targeted raids. We should be able to reach at least one more destination before they do.

Our skirmishes against the Faridun's outriders have gone well, but their so-called King has made moves of his own while we have protected your flank. You may very well find that he has ridden ahead of us, but we must still try.

As the tale-women spread word of our victories with my name lauded, I find myself growing stronger. This must be the beginnings of Divinity. I will use this strength to defeat the King of the Faridun. Perhaps it will even be enough to destroy the Seed of Corruption.

You have done as well as can be expected on your own, <italic>{jingakh}. It will soon be time for our goals to coincide. Many other <italic>{akharas} have heard of our victories, but more have suffered from the sudden tide of Corruption. Our distant sisters have chosen to join the war to defeat this would-be King and destroy the Seed of Corruption.\r\n\r\nThe Faridun have assembled a tremendous Dreadnought far larger than any one caravan. As we speak, it is barreling through the heart of the Vastiri, leaving devastation in its wake. The Faridun seem to have some unknown destination in mind, but we intend to converge our <italic>{akharas} upon them before they can reach it. Join the pursuit. There will undoubtedly be creatures of Corruption in the wake of the Dreadnought.

The time has come for a final confrontation. The Faridun have united, but for the first time in many generations, the Maraketh have as well. I intend to infiltrate the Dreadnought and face the Perennial King myself. If I defeat him in personal combat, I can end this war. The Faridun and the Maraketh alike will witness my victory. That will be my chance to unify them under one banner. I can feel myself on the verge of some great transformation... and so, too, will my people transform, should we win the day. Glory will be ours again, <italic>{jingakh}. I want you by my side for this final battle, for the King will no doubt be supported by legions of Corrupted abominations.\r\n\r\nThe future beckons. Are you prepared?

The future is now ours to mold. It has been thousands of years since the Maraketh were united enough to create a new goddess, and I am honoured to become their divine Sekhema of Sekhemas. I am finally able to deliver the return to glory that I have always promised.\r\n\r\nI understand that you wish to continue pursuing the Seed of Corruption. We will assist you when the task of solidifying our new unity is complete.
The Maraketh will destroy the Seed. The Maraketh will destroy <italic>{you!}
Not so mortal as you expect!
Then force of arms must do. <italic>{Jingakh}, we fight!
We must defeat the King before we pursue the Seed!
I am your new Sekhema of Sekhemas. I am your Goddess. With the power you have given me, I grant amnesty to the Faridun, should they surrender and agree to follow me. We are now... one people.
The day is won, my friend. You are a foreigner no longer. For fighting at my side, I consider you one of us. Let us return home.

That foreigner escaped with the Seed of Corruption, but my outriders have found their trail. It leads away from the path that I must follow for now. There are some among the Faridun and the Maraketh who refuse my rule. I must unite the Vastiri Plains under a single leader if we are to restore this land to its former glory. I assume you will choose to part from us here and pursue the Seed. I understand that choice. I will send reinforcements to help you when the unification is over. Until then, I wish you luck in the Wastes to which the enemy has escaped.
What would you have me do?
Our way of life is <italic>{built} on force.
To change our way of life would be to erase ourselves. You knew what we were when you asked for our help.
My faithful friend. I believe you should take your shade home. He has developed a grievance against us for things we have always done.

I do not desire to overcome it. I give myself up to the will of my people. I live for <italic>{them}. I will manifest their dreams upon these very sands. Conquest, domination, and power - these have always been Maraketh values. That has not changed. Only our capability has grown.
So be it. You have chosen to betray us!
My people's faith burns through me!
Ugh! You sting... Like the scorpion!
Ugh! You sting... Like the scorpion!
I have not yet... Earned my rest!
After all this time, this was who they sent?
Oh. I will... Keep waiting then.

Allow me to repay you for freeing me from my imprisonment. By my right as Djinn, I invite you to participate in the Trial of the Sekhemas. There, I can earn my rest, and you may prove yourself worthy of the wisdom of the Maraketh.
Take me... To the Sekhemas' proving grounds...
We're not done yet... We are called upon by fate...
I've already waited thousands of years. What's a few more?
Here, you must prove yourself. My barya, my coin, will grant you access. \r\n

This is the tale as it was told to me by our <italic>{akhara}'s tale-woman before me, and as told to her by the tale-woman before her. These words have remained unchanged since the beginning. <continue>Many thousands of years ago, we were a simple people. Hunters. Roamers. We moved valley to valley in search of meat and berries. There was none of the discipline we know today, but that was about to change. These fair plains became barren and lightless, a time those generations called the Winter of the World. <continue>One thousand years of ice brought hardship and suffering, but that was only the beginning. To the south, the foreign tyrant Ahn fell, and horrible creatures flooded forth under this darkness, seemingly born of bone and blood and foul magic. Survival meant banding together and creating the strict traditions that eventually became what we know today. To fight was to live. Disorder meant death. <continue>In the darkest depths of that era, when hope was but a memory, the twin sister Sekhemas Solerai and Lundara arose to unite our scattered peoples for the first time. They wielded the essence of gold and silver, gleaming with such ferocity that the grey skies had no choice but to give way. <continue>The creatures retreated under the sands, never to be seen again, and our fair plains blazed with emerald forests and sapphire rivers. This brought about the most glorious age of our people. A time of conquest, wealth, great heroes, and gods that lasted for another thousand years. <continue>But then, one fell winter... the gods vanished. Our beloved Garukhan was the last to succumb, holding on for two moons against a powerful enervation. She gave what final orders she could, mandated our traditions be upheld, and then went silent. <continue>The Maraketh were not disturbed. We did not lose hope. We knew who we were, and those values had not left us with the departure of the gods. When the sky burned, when the Vaal fell, when the Eternals came and sought to be our masters, and then fell as well, we endured. <continue>We have protected these fair plains for three hundred and four generations, and we will continue to do so for another three hundred and four. That is our duty, and our birthright.

Since we do not have forty-five spare hours, I suppose I could tell you a small piece of one of Sekhema of Sekhemas Orbala's adventures. <continue>Her second adventure took place three moons before her dance with the scorpion. She was not a Sekhema at that time, not even a <i>{dekhara}. Word had not spread of her first adventure yet, either, for only her sister knew of the bandit-chase for Solerai's Spear that ended with Stridevolf in flames, so at that time she was still unknown. <continue>For that reason, she initially said nothing when a visiting Vaal dignitary insulted her mother. He was a devotee of Arakaali, and wished to indulge in unmentionable activities. When Orbala's mother rejected him, he spoke vile words, then departed. <continue>Orbala could not let this stand. She crept from her home in the dark of the night, tracking the dignitary's entourage through many unfamiliar forest roads. She found him bathing at the foot of Keth's second river, Halani. Aiming true, she struck him through the throat with a single arrow. <continue>It was then that his entourage appeared and explained that he had merely been a Maraketh spy playing a role, and that his insult had been intended to spread his reputation ahead of his passage. <continue>Orbala was given a choice: to face the justice of the Plains for her slaying of this important agent, or to don his clothes and fulfill his mission, masquerading as a Vaal dignitary in his place, so that the Sekhemas might assess threats on the border between the two peoples. <continue>She succeeded in her ruse through many dangerous and humorous situations, although this adventure also ended with Lira Vaal in flames.
A brave request, but that is rather a long tale! I do not have five uninterrupted days to tell it. Perhaps, ask again after this conflict is over?

I am sorry, <italic>{jingakh}. I do not believe I have the strength to tell that harrowing tale right now. I must use what time I have left to teach my tales to Risu. Perhaps one day, she will tell it to you.
Here we are. You may disembark from that side. Guards! Lower the ramp!
You offer yourself as a gift for the Seed, how generous!
I do not think so, mortal.
The Seed feasts upon your divine folly.

...I believe in the Twilight Order's supposed cause, I simply don't trust them. Outsiders can never understand the Ezomyte struggle. Our songs and stories go back to the very Winter of the World, when we were but savages clawing grubs from the dirt of what would one day be Ezomyr. We have always fought for survival, for home, for hearth. That is the bloodline I am proud of, stretching back thousands of years.\r\n\r\nBut as I sit in the crimson light of this strange Seed, I wonder if I have made the right choice. That dark being we accosted and strung up at the Twilight Order's behest seemed to be some sort of caretaker for this living oddity. I know nothing of this Seed, and now it rests in the heart of my Manor. Am I the right man for this? Is my bloodline strong enough to contain this abomination? If only I knew for certain...

...Even after six hours on the rack, the Provost refuses to give me the names of the men who escaped from their own failed coup attempt. Does he not realise the machinations of shapechangers are at work here? I do not doubt Connal's loyalty, only his intellect.

The shapechangers are obvious in their tactics. They are untrained in the art of deception. They fidget. They sweat. They are constantly afraid of being singled out or questioned. That is how I identify them.

They are less than human. A human being is winsome, even beautiful, but these creatures bely that recognition of kin. The closer I look, the more I see that they are no more than bones carrying bags of flesh under an oozing membrane of skin. Peel away that covering, and the disgusting truth is revealed. They must be thrown into the pit and out of sight. Let the Seed consume those flayed abominations...
I tried to seek peace, and the Sekhemas disgraced me! Left my corpse to rot in the sand! This time, we choose war.
I shall dethrone you sekhema... And leave you to the sands!
I shall dethrone you sekhema... And leave you to the sands!
The Maraketh will fall... By my hand!
The Maraketh will fall... By my hand!
The Maraketh shall be purged from the desert... Mark my words!
The Maraketh shall be purged from the desert... Mark my words!
You waste your time... And mine!
You waste your time... And mine!
The trail of Corruption leads east, so east we shall go, to the Plains of Vastiri...
[DNT] Now that the darkness has been driven back, we can reach Ogham's boats. They'll get you across the water to the shores of the Vastiri Plains.

So, your shade is actually the Thief of Virtue. I suspected as much. There are many conflicting accounts of what happened to cause the return - and death - of the gods, but one thing is true in all of the rumours. He played an important role. <continue>I refer you to Orbala's great adventures. Every single one of her tales ends with at least one city in ruins... but she is still a hero, and we still remember her fondly, because her intent was noble. As the tale goes, the vine climbs towards the sun for light. It does not mean to crumble the wall. <continue>It is much like this desert. We are not in denial about how it has changed. We see that it was once verdant, and we know that it will one day be so again. Devastation always heals, given enough time, and perhaps the Thief of Virtue will eventually forgive himself as well.
We shall wait here, <i>{jingakh}, but the military carts have departed for the Gates. Make haste!
What if the Faridun attack your flank through the lower pass?

We did send a single <i>{dekhara} to the island of Ogham to glean what clues we can about Corruption. She verified much of what your shade told us, and brought back a few tales as well. <continue>It seems you are a natural fit for the mercenary role you serve with us, given that you did the same in Ogham for their legendary hero, Finn. <continue>New Ezomyte myths are rare in these parts. The other tale-women will be quite impressed when I tell them how Finn saved Ogham and built a grand treetop mansion in which to house and feed his loyal vassals. <continue>How unbelievable! A fortress <i>{in the trees?} I've hardly seen a single healthy tree in my time, but Ogham is covered with trunks as tall as the Ancient Gates themselves! Whole forests, and rivers, too! Truly, a wondrous land.
Indeed, and it dragged out Keth's fading for several hundred years. It became a vulnerability, a target for raiders and conquest. Best to put a wounded beast down.
What else can you tell me of Garukhan?
Yes, but their location has been guarded well.
A tale-woman would die before divulging her secrets.
The other <i>{akharas} are calling you the Hand of the Ardura.
That is not for me to determine, young one.
As you should, unless someone more capable emerges.
Of course, young one. There is always another story. The new moon approaches.
That is not the tale I usually tell on the new moon, but perhaps adjustments can be made!
Do the Faridun have any tales?
That doesn't sound likely. Poison is underhanded and dishonourable.
The Perennial King has the Seed. Your outriders will become confused when they draw near its influence.
I am curious, what led to Keth's decline?
Was any attempt made to irrigate and conserve water?
I suppose it could be looked at that way...
I've likely said this before, but I was captivated by her. Not just by her appearance, which Divinity crafted for her, but by the fierceness of her soul.
A dark shadow has fallen across the land...
Continue the assault! Slay them all!
Onwards! Give these demons no quarter!
That was for my fallen sisters.
The Faridun can produce worthy champions after all...
My fallen sisters will be remembered.
The Faridun have fallen to corruption. Their eyes gleam with madness!
The final gate is broken! We must continue our advance!
Make haste, he must not escape!
Quickly! He conjures the very sands against us!
We cannot follow through the raging sands. Let us return to the caravan and question this defector.
You received the death you deserved! And I shall give you another!
Feel the chill of the grave!
Feel the chill of the grave!
Feel the chill of the grave!
This is our land, we stand united!
Sleep in ice, wake in snow. Sleep my pretties as you grow...
Sleep in ice, wake in snow. Sleep my pretties as you grow...

I do know a way out. If we fail, and the Empire falls, I have one last resort. I fear it, but it is my last hope. 

We imprisoned Ichlotl the Blackjaw in a Soul Core, alone, for his crimes. Isolated like that, without any other souls in the lattice, his stone form seemed to retain much of his personality. Do I dare drain my own lifeblood into something we used as a punishment worse than death? 

We have toiled so long to defeat death, all I know now is fear... if the sky turns to blood, if flames consume Utzaal, only then will I decide.

The Orok are truly terrifying to behold. I suspect their canine features result from genetic mutations, perhaps borne of the Cataclysms that reshaped these lands. <continue>Their tribesmen are savage — I rarely leave their territories without scars to show for it — yet they hold a knowledge we Oriathans have long since abandoned. Our 'high-born' civilization prides itself on its advancements but remains woefully primitive in matters of the spirit and the natural world. <continue>For all their brutality, the Orok live in harmony with the forces of nature. Perhaps they have no choice, but I wonder if we are the fools for believing we've transcended it. Better to live with nature than to die defying it.

We strayed from the route marked on our map, driven further afield by painted men with savage intent. <continue>Tonight, for reasons I cannot fathom, we have been granted a brief reprieve. Our hunters halted at the edge of this marsh, unwilling to pursue. They watched from the trees as we threaded the narrow band of solid ground between desert and swamp. I know not what they fear, but we must brave the unknown if we are to reach the encampment at the Ziggurat. <continue>Through my spyglass, I see nothing ahead. The waters lie still, and the muddy banks between seem clear. Yet my nerves burn with the unmistakable sense of being watched. There is no one... no thing... but this silence feels alive. We have no choice but to run for it.

"For centuries, our people have been conducting experimental breeding programs in order to expand our empire and further our knowledge. Some may refer to it as 'playing god', but I know that the true gods smile upon us when we experiment with nature, for we are emulating their processes of creation and destruction. Our most recent creations were once considered to be mere dreams, but we made them a reality, and so we named them 'Chimerals'.

The Chimerals are among our finest undertakings, for they possess immeasurable beauty and serve well as our pets. The Chimera, however, was a hideous experiment gone wrong – and yet it is still a wonder to behold; a fantastical and savage beast which can barely be contained, let alone slain.

How did we achieve such mastery over nature, you ask? Through thaumaturgy; through the raw, red energy of corruption itself, which enabled us to bend genetics to our will."

– Zalatl, Architect of Thaumaturgy
Oh, hello. I'm Alva Valai. We can always use another pair of hands around here. <continue>Be sure to talk to Oswald as he <i>{usually} likes to greet newcomers. In any case, welcome!
I'm sorry, but I'm really very busy. But if you are interested in helping us find relics, Oswald can show you the ropes.

The ziggurat beneath us was once the Temple of the Sun God, one of the oldest built in the city of Utzaal's religious district. It was in active use for at least a thousand years, but when the Vaal Cataclysm struck, the city flooded, presumably killing everyone inside. <continue>Good thing for us, because this lake is the only reason it hasn't been ransacked by other treasure hunters already. One man's mass death is... another man's treasure, I suppose.

What kind of stunt was that, traversing the Marsh? Have to be smarter if you're to survive. As Quartermaster, I'll do my best to keep you alive. <continue>I can buy what equipment you find, or sell you what others have unearthed before we ship it back to Kingsmarch. If you disappear in the jungle, I'll also be the one to note your death in our logs. You're welcome.
I'd stay well away from them, if I were you. The Azakh-Kul use a variety of poisons to disable unwary adventurers. You might speak to our guide, Servi, who has been working on some antidotes.
She sounded... Well, filthy. I don't know how those Treasure Hunters made it in there, but I sure feel for them. We all know risk is part of the job but... What a way to go. Boggles the mind really.
Utzaal is close. Be careful. The Vaal heavily relied on the use of corruption. Their lands may still be dangerous.

From memory, somewhere in this region, there were sophisticated canals and waterways. We might be able to use them to drain this lake. We must hope that the mechanisms are still functioning, despite their age. It is the only way to reverse the drowning of this once thriving city... the first step in our search for the secret knowledge of the Vaal.

It is strange to return to this place of my divine youth and see it so aged and forgotten. When I was here, the Vaal were the height of civilisation, and their future was bright.<continue>They had their problems, like any other people, but I thought I could free them from the moral hazards of Divinity by removing gods from the equation.<continue>While we are here, I would like to discover whether this ruination is my fault, or whether something else happened to them...

Because we have lost the trail of the Seed of Destruction, our only hope is to seek the knowledge of those who studied the Beast for centuries: the Vaal. I know something of the Beast's creation myself... but I was asleep while it was actually alive. There is only one Vaal city left intact after two thousand years, and that is where we must go. In my wanderings these last twenty years, I have seen evidence that a Vaal scientist was working on an incredibly powerful device intended to defend his people against a potential Cataclysm. Obviously, it wasn't completed in time... but perhaps we can pick up where he left off.

Utzaal is the last intact Vaal city, for a reason that will also be our greatest hurdle. During the first Cataclysm, the city was flooded, killing most of its population and burying its wealth under a valley of water. Corruption has since poisoned that water, making it impossible for anyone to loot the city. From my time in Utzaal when I was young, I do have some idea how to solve this problem... we shall speak again when we find it.

You have found the Waterways? Search it for a control mechanism. Vaal technology, at least in that era, was based on engraved stonework and latent systems of channeled energy. It should be operational, even after all this time... drain the city, and let us see what ancient secrets Utzaal has kept protected for us.

Returning with Doryani was an inspired move. As the foremost expert on the Beast that ever lived, he is exactly the man we need. 

<continue>I doubt we can trust him in a broader sense, but, for the moment, our goals are aligned. He wishes to contain the Beast, and so do we. 

<continue>If he thinks we should travel south to Ngamakanui, then so we shall. This weapon of the Precursors... it may just be our best hope...

You the one who waded through the undead in the Marsh, eh? Truly, you need a guide. Luck's on your side today, friend. I am such a guide. Maybe... I can help you survive... <continue>Not all tribes in this region are so friendly. You would be wise to listen to me on the dangers of the jungle. Yes... you are lucky, indeed.

Apus is my grandson. Can you believe that? A young spry thing like me, a grandmother? Ha ha ha!... Don't be answerin' that. <continue>Apus inherited my son's rowdy spirit. Maybe it's a family curse. We have always been the type to do what we shouldn't... like helping outsiders, such as yourself. <continue>One day, he'll be a great man, just like his father. Until then, I try to keep him safe.

<i>{Everything} here can kill you. A snake you can't see, a strange plant... even one of your own. Survival in the jungle depends upon learning the lessons from those who died before you. <continue> That's the wisdom of my tribe, and since these treasure hunters pay me so well, I don't mind sharin'. Hah hah! <continue>Any place you want to know about, come to me with questions and I'll tell you what I know.
Ah yes, we've come across this before, but we can't power it...

The Vaal used this device to operate the mechanisms in the canal, but we would need a special artifact to power it. From the translations I've made, I believe they were called 'Soul Cores'. <continue>I've never even seen an intact Soul Core large enough for something like this though... I suppose if you want to try and find one you could ask our guide, Servi.

Death gems, blood crystals... Or more colloquially 'Soul Cores'. They were made by sacrificing living people and capturing their energies inside a crystal lattice. <continue>Some think the victims are still trapped inside, existing in eternal agony until someone drains the core's energy completely. <continue>There's no way to know that for certain, of course, but it's rather chilling to think about...

These waterways are a series of canals the Vaal built on the upper edge of the city. The great Matlan river didn't run quite this far south, but they diverted a portion of it for a complex irrigation system. <continue>That really allowed the city to thrive and the Vaal to flourish. Though I don't fully understand why they created a system that could flood the entire city...

The Wetlands are breeding grounds for the jungle's most vicious creatures. Pretty, it's true, with colours like sunshine in rain... but deadly all the same. <continue>Plenty a fool treasure hunter head there, but never return - least not alive. Watch out for the flowers that move without a breeze. Them are serpents, hidin' in the jungle, spittin' poison. <continue>A massive flyin' beast hunts that place. Some say it got the head of a lion, others say it looks like a Gorebeast. Some talk 'bout a tail like a Maraketh scorpion. <continue>But the truth? It doesn't matter. None from my tribe have set foot there in forty-three seasons.
So this is the source of the Azakh-Kul poison!

So this the source of the Orok poison! Long time ago, this crypt was a resting place for the Vaal. But since their time, the Orok come here to worship the Three-Headed Snake. Even them couldn't survive her poison. <continue>This venom... You have found the dark heart of the Orok wickedness. If those savages can learn to use it, maybe I can too. Let me see...
Heh heh. Drink this. A foul brew, but you'll thank me... if you survive.
Now this is a find! A Vaal ruin that hasn't been looted. No one from camp has managed to make it to this part of the jungle and survive... Until now!
This mechanism... if powered with a small Soul Core, it could open that door. There should definitely be Soul Cores somewhere around here. They had to power these constructs somehow!
Look for a red crystal a bit bigger than your fist. It should be warm to the touch... Why, you ask? That'd be the soul trapped inside.

Near the end of their civilisation, the Vaal tried to combat a worsening labour shortage - by sacrificing their own citizens to power constructs. Designed to till the fields, mine the quarries and the like - they were quite a marvel. <continue>As it turns out, human souls don't make for a very sustainable fuel source... And so began their downward spiral. Rather silly for such an intellectual people, wouldn't you say?
Oh, did you fight some sort of animal on the way here? Servi did tell us that the Wetlands had quite a few nasty beasts. But hey... I bet you didn't even break a sweat!
Well... Consider me impressed! I'll keep investigating here for now. If you find anything interesting, I'll come to you.
This is the largest Soul Core I've ever seen! With this we could power the mechanism in the waterways. But it isn't charged...

There is still latent energy residing here... From what I can gather, these lines in the stonework should lead to generators. You might need to find some more Soul Cores to spin them up, but everything looks to be in surprisingly decent condition. <continue>Maybe the constructs have been maintaining all this... In any case, let's hope it still functions. We'll then have to remove that large Soul Core from the wall of course, but that shouldn't be a problem.
The Soul Core is charged! Why don't you do the honours?
Oh dear. Now we just have to remove it from the giant construct... Good luck!
Wow! You did it! Now we can use that Soul Core to power the mechanisms in the waterways. Good job with that construct, by the way.

Hello there, I'm Alva Valai. Sorry about Oswald... He can be a bit... Rough with newcomers. But he's really not a bad sort. <continue>In any case, we can always use another pair of hands around here. Welcome!

Something tells me you're the exploring type - we've got that in common. But some places even I steer clear of... I rather enjoy being alive, you see. <continue>Still, if you're feeling adventurous, there's fortunes to be made out there in the wilds. I'm especially interested in all things related to the Vaal, for academic reasons of course... but a bit of treasure never goes amiss.

From my understanding, it was a failsafe. A way to make sure their creations didn't get the better of them... Or the world. The Vaal really were a very intelligent and pragmatic people, you know. <continue>At the south east edge of the city, there is a large dam. I've spent months trying to find a way to release the outer spillways... But to no avail. Those very walls are what keep the city flooded to this day.

This looks like the workshop of Jiquani, the Vaal Architect of Industry. He masterminded the constructs designed to help his people keep pace with their own rapid expansion. <continue>As with many of the Architects, his methods were brutal, to say the least. Countless peasants sacrificed at the altar of progress. Their screams still echo inside the soul cores themselves. Gosh... Quite grim, isn't it?

The members of this expedition seem to believe the Ziggurat beneath our feet holds an ancient device that was intended to be used against the Cataclysm that destroyed the Vaal.\r\n<continue>The source of that Cataclysm was the previous Beast... which means the device below may be exactly what we need to stop the new one. Find your way into the Ziggurat, and let us see what the greatest minds of the Vaal Empire created.\r\n<continue>If they didn't manage to complete it in time, maybe we can finish their work...

This portal provides an opportunity that I had never considered. To consult the greatest minds of the Vaal directly.\r\n<continue>Enter the portal. Find their experts on the Beast, or on Corruption. They may know of ways to control corruption that even I am not aware of.

Be warned, friend. The waterways on the Matlan river be a barrier between us and the Azak tribe. The Orok may be trouble, but the Azak... them a true horror. <continue>Their queen-witch, Ignagduk, takes a child every blood moon night. Why, I won't guess. If you trespass, only death awaits you. But if you survive, while you are there... please, rip out her <i>{heart!}

You slain the Beastmaster? You are truly the shadow of death! With that kind of strength, you could deal the Azak tribe a deadly blow. Beyond this place, that's where them make their home.  <continue>Their queen-witch, Ignagduk... she must die. She take a child from my tribe every blood moon, and keeps their spirit trapped. Free them, and we reward you as best we can.
You are confident, I give you that. Do you truly believe you can beat the Azak tribe? Do so, and my people would be forever grateful. Slay Ignagduk and free the spirits of our stolen children!
You have slain the Bog Witch? Then you have healed a wound on the heart of my people. Today, these swamps be blessed by a touch of sunlight.
At last, Utzaal's temple district! Untold wealth lies in wait below!

You drained the entire lake? I was going to ship in some Kalguuran explosives, but that's one way to get into these temples, I suppose. <continue>Oh. Alva's found something. She's waiting for you at the base of these stairs. I'd join you, but I'm not sure how much I trust two-thousand-year-old waterways to keep the city dry. You enjoy yourself.
Unbroken statues! Original brickwork! The glimmer of gold! Oh, we're gonna be rich!

Beneath our feet is the Temple of the Sun God, Kopec. It was said to contain a grand device. I've seen writings by a fellow named Ketzuli that mention his research in this temple, but I can't quite make sense of what the device was or how it functioned. <continue>We can't use Kalguuran explosives without risking whatever's in there, so we'd have to drain the city to be able to get inside.

Beyond this sealed door is the Temple of the Sun God, Kopec. I've seen writings by a fellow named Ketzuli that mention his research in this temple, but I can't quite make sense of what the device was or how it functioned. Unfortunately we can't use Kalguuran explosives without risking whatever's inside. <continue>However... there's a piece missing from the door. Knowing the Vaal, it'll be made of gold, of course! <continue>I recommend heading into the city to search for it. Try looking around the Aggorat area, as that was well known for its opulence and golden tributes, especially at the main temple's apex. Hurry back if you find it!

It seems there is a piece missing from the door... Something in the shape of a small statue. Knowing the Vaal, it'll be made of gold, of course. <continue>I suggest venturing into the city to look for it. Focus on the Aggorat area, renowned for its grandeur and golden adornments, particularly at the apex of its main temple. Hurry back if you find it!

It's hard to guess what the device inside the Temple might be. I do know that it was commissioned by Queen Atziri's Thaumaturge, Doryani himself. The project was given all the resources it needed, and the work was kept secret, even from Atziri. <continue>As best as I could translate, they claimed using it might mean 'abandoning all they had built'. They seemed to view it as a last resort, a way to save their legacy if all else failed... It's not often I detect fear in Vaal writings, but they definitely hoped they would never have to use it.

By their final days, the Vaal were a deeply tiered empire based on brutal competition. Those at the top vied with each other through any means necessary, and Doryani was the foremost among these ambitious and amoral men. <continue>He was second only to Queen Atziri herself. Utzaal was the seat of his power, and ancient writings claim he undertook a vast array of strange projects and sordid experiments here... Some glyphs I have seen are too stomach-turning to discuss.

How do I even begin to describe the last Queen of the Vaal? She left a tremendous mark on history. She was intelligent and capable enough to rule unquestioned over a bloodthirsty empire of volatile nobles, and the people adored her and feared her in equal measure. <continue>Vaal writings speak of her as the most beautiful woman of the era, but also the most dangerous. She sought eternal life, and she was willing to sacrifice <i>{anything} to achieve it. The ruins around you are the consequence of those ambitions. <continue>Sometimes while I'm looting a temple, I remember that everything we find once belonged to a living, breathing person that probably died horribly... Sort of takes the fun out of it, doesn't it?
You found it! Try placing the idol in the door... Maybe we'll get lucky!
What is that strange heat? Is it possible that something has survived within after all this time?
Ouch, that's hot! I'm gonna stay here for now. See if you can find a way past that heat!
This chamber gives me a very strange feeling...
These runes... I can make out a symbol for 'blood' and 'waiting'... hmm...
Oh wait, it's not 'a blood offering,' it's 'someone of Vaal blood'...
Is this a good time to mention I have a distant Vaal ancestor?! Perhaps if I...
We're back in the Encampment? We were right on top of this device the entire time!
It's some sort of... gateway... how incredible!
Are these... living Vaal? In the flesh?!
Hello! My name is Alva Valai! It was I who -
It's been a lot longer than that.
It's been nearly two thousand years since the Cataclysm.
History recorded the number of survivors who made it to the Azmeri in the mountains... three thousand, one hundred, and twenty-six.
Release me, and we can talk about this. We'll figure something out.
You're here! There is so much you need to understand!
Stop it! Why are you fighting?! You both want the same thing!
Thanks for the rescue, but you two need to talk!
You really need to speak with Doryani. I think you both want the same thing: to prevent a Cataclysm.
You <i>{know} why we're here! It happened! It cannot be stopped!
Well... That was quite the adventure. I'll take you to Kingsmarch so you can charter a ship and search for the weapon that Doryani spoke of. We can leave whenever you're ready, just let me know.
It's a long overland journey to Kingsmarch, but there shouldn't be too much danger once we leave the jungle. The Kalguurans keep the road reasonably secure. Shall we?

That man is a mystery. Though it appears he is on your side for now, you mustn't forget who he is and all he has done... There is something eerily cold and calculating about him. <continue>I believe he will aid you so long as your goals align with his. The moment they do not... I'm just saying, don't turn your back on him.

This little excursion here represents my lifelong ambition. It's not just about finding treasure. I want to build an entire archaeological society someday! Wraeclast has countless layers of history buried beneath it, and I aim to uncover every last bit. <continue>I intend to call my group 'the Reliquarians.' A bit ostentatious, but the best things should be! A shame I couldn't have founded it a few decades ago, back when my birthplace Oriath was still a thriving city. <continue>Thanks to the Templars, relics from a dozen different cultures found their way to that little island over the centuries and are now all lost thanks to the disasters that happened there...

Oswald's a grim sort, isn't he? He's always 'injury this, death that'. Personally, I've never been hurt while treasure hunting. I actually find it rather easy! <continue>He always makes sure we have the proper supplies, and checks his lists for everything four or five times before we make a move. He also invented what I call the Oswald technique. On the rare occasions he personally goes out with us, he throws a rock at absolutely everything before touching it. Every flagstone, every pillar, every statue... <continue>You'd be positively amazed at the elaborate traps he sets off, even in places I've walked through already!

Servi has been a fantastic ally to us here. Her people have lived in the vicinity of Utzaal for countless generations, so she's been able to show us all the most interesting Vaal ruins. <continue>The accessible ruins were all looted long ago, of course, but the lake around us has protected most of the city since the end of the Vaal empire...

That hooded fellow over there... He's a friend of yours, I take it? Seems to be one of few words. <continue>Oh well. I'm not one to judge the company you choose to keep. Oswald's going to lose his wits if any more of you show up though!

So you're looking for a device the Vaal intended to use against the Cataclysm? Ah, so that's why you came here. Well... You're on the right trail. The Ziggurat on which we stand was rumored to contain a device to save their people. <continue>If you want to explore it, you'll have to find a way to drain the city first.
History says Doryani disappeared just before the Cataclysm. Now we know why—he came with us to the present. It seems the choice has already been made.

I've heard of the Beast. Everyone has. If someone is truly trying to raise another, then they must be the grandest of fools. These very ruins around us are the result of an attempt to control such a thing. This is the only way it can end.
The Vaal in this pyramid must have been trapped here since the Cataclysm. Was it Corruption that kept them alive? Or the energy from their sun? I can't imagine a worse fate...
That sun is an incredible achievement, no doubt, but it doesn't fit with what the Vaal wrote about this place. Perhaps it powers the device we seek...
Don't worry, I can solve this. This is all just a misunderstanding!
Why, that was me, of course! I am Alva Valai, treasure hunter extraordinaire—
[DNT] Good work on capturing Doryani. Let's meet up inside The Ziggurat Refuge at the base of this encampment.
Hurry! I'm being held in the farthest chamber—
I don't think they'll mind if I take this! For... archaeological purposes!

Seventy-four shipments of Soul Cores in the span of three moons. Seventy-four shipments... and it still won't be enough, if our fears become realized. 

We have put our lives on the line because Doryani asked us to do so. I accept this and... I am not a traitor to the Queen, but, sometimes, loyalty requires protecting her from her own mistakes. 

We need more time. We just need more time!

I log everything here, so I can catalogue the thousands of ways to die the jungle offers. If you can, be sure to write some sort of final entry detailing how you die. A death log won't benefit you, of course, but it will certainly benefit me. <continue>I don't mean to be overly fatalistic, but the amateurs coming from Kingsmarch are accomplishing nothing but feeding the Chimerals. The most I can do, as Quartermaster, is ensure they're equipped for exploration. That's where the real profit in treasure hunting is, you see. <continue>I don't go out there if I can help it. I'm the unluckiest man alive. Yet, I'm the wealthiest in this camp. You have to be good when you're trading with the Kalguurans, or they'll fleece you.

Ah, Kingsmarch, so called by the Kalguurans. They're newcomers to Wraeclast, about twenty years now. They're traders by nature. In fact, they've partially funded this very expedition. <continue>For some reason, they're very interested in Vaal artefacts. We ship most of what we find back to Kingsmarch, and they pay handsomely for it.

So, the city of Utzaal has been laid bare to the world after all these centuries. I know you're after some particular device, but I can't help but remind you that we are here for a purpose of our own. <continue>Treasure hunters hunt treasure, yeah? I'll not be the first to set foot in those deadly sunken ruins, but if you're braving them, you might as well keep an eye out for anything that looks... valuable. <continue>In particular, look for buildings with Monkey statues on 'em. If you spy something like that, give me a shout. I'll be waiting with... great anticipation.

I'm no storyteller, but I know what's what. The monkey represented Kamasa, the Vaal god of Wealth. <continue>If you see a statue of a monkey, it means treasure. It may be a vault. May be a temple. Could be a vast forge. Any of the above would mean fabulous riches.

Came back alive, did you? I'll organise the men. We'll start carting the gold out of there. No sign of ol' Kamasa, eh? Then he won't miss it. <continue>Keep anything you were able to lift out of there yourself. Let's call it a finders fee. I'm feeling generous today, considering we actually found treasure, and all came out alive.

That's it! Kamasa! The Monkey God! Even <i>{I'm} tempted to... no, no, I'll just die horribly. It's you that's got to go in there. Give a look around. If you find what I <i>{think} you'll find, and if you clear out any dangers, we're all going to leave this place rich.

Now you've done it. Why are you making me risk my hide by coming out here? Wait—look! You lucky madman! The Monkey God! <continue>The monkey represented Kamasa, the Vaal god of Wealth. Even <i>{I'm} tempted to... no, no, I'll just die horribly. It's <i>{you} that's got to go in there. <continue>Give a look around. If you find what I <i>{think} you'll find, and if you clear out any dangers, we're all going to leave this place rich.

Little is known about the Monkey God. He was initially portrayed as curious, wise, and prone to mischief. His cult's core values became exploitation and ambition. <continue>His high priests eventually ran everything remotely financial in the Empire. I can only imagine what treasures are hidden in their ancient coffers...

The jungle's not even the worst of your worries over there. On the other side of the waterways, you'll find a fierce tribe - the Azak. Them turn animals into savage monsters... real beastmasters, but wicked to the core. Tread careful 'round them.

The coward. <continue>Evil in the shadows, my friend. Evil in the shadows. If you find the source of their wickedness, you let me know. I must see it for myself to make an antidote.

The jungle ruins are full of deadly creatures, you know. Quadrillas can tear a man apart in seconds - but at least you can hear them comin'. The real danger? The apes that drop down from above. <continue>Life is plenty here, thrivin' for generations, but death always comes for the careless.

This, then, will be our new home until our promised land is made real.

The promised land is bountiful, a blissful place overflowing with potential. My brethren surround me... We are one, experiencing the entirety of time all at once. Even as I write this, I am on the cusp of transcendence; the script before my eyes morphs into illegible symbols, and I cannot stop laughing... rejoicing at the bright future that I know us to all share.

I remember the before-times. We bowed before Atziri, who bowed before no-one. But Mother is the one true Queen. She is the one who brings solace. She is the one who grows gifts for us. We must keep eating them, for they bring pure delight...
Mother is love. Mother is life. Feasting brings visions. Eternal life. Queen reigns still, ours, and theirs, under sky of blood. Feasting shows us. Feasting brings smile.

Twenty years is a very long time to search for something.
